align_content.description: How a container that wraps spreads its lines across its direction, and a `grid` its rows, where they leave room: `stretch` shares the room among them

align_items.description: Where a container puts its children across its own direction, and a `grid` each child in its cell down: `stretch` makes each as wide (or tall) as the container, `baseline` lines up their first lines of text, the others keep each child's own size

direction.description: Which way this subtree runs: `right_to_left` lays it out as its mirror image (a row and a grid's columns start at the right edge, `start` and `end` swap, and so do the left and right of a padding, a margin and an inset), `left_to_right` keeps it unmirrored inside a mirrored UI (a board of Latin letters in Arabic), and `auto` takes its parent's, which at a root is the locale's (`strings.right_to_left`)

fit.description: Class words, in order, that a `row` or a `column` puts in force one after another until what it holds fits on one line along its direction, the ones before kept: `["icon", "small", "name"]`. What it holds then answers each by its role's table of that name. Keeps it on one line, whatever `wrap_children` says. Empty takes its role's `fit`

gap.description: Space between a container's children, across and down, in design pixels: a row puts the first between its children and the second between the lines it wraps onto, a column the second between its children, and a grid the first between its columns and the second between its rows. Below zero on an axis takes the theme's own, which is 8 where it says nothing, and a stated zero puts them edge to edge

justify.description: How a container spreads its children along its own direction once they have their sizes, and a `grid` its columns: `stretch` grows a grid's `auto` columns into the room, and in a row or a column is `start`

min_lines.description: How many lines a wrapping container divides its children between at least: `balance` evens them over this many, and any wrap shares a known cross size among them

reverse.description: Lay a `row` or a `column`'s children out from its far end

splitter_width.description: How wide a grab the seams between this container's children get, in design pixels; 0 leaves them fixed. A drag writes the new size onto the neighbour that states one

wrap_children.description: Whether a container's children run onto more lines when they do not fit: `none` keeps them on one line, `wrap` starts a line when the row is full, `balance` evens the lines out over at least `min_lines`, and a `_reverse` word stacks the lines the other way

draggable.description: Let a drag carry a card of a `list` with `grid_columns` out of it, drawn under the pointer; `dropped` says which card was let go

grid_columns.description: How many columns a `list` flows its cards into, in the words a `grid`'s `grid_columns` takes; empty draws a line a row

reorderable.description: Let a drag move a row of a `list` or a `tree`. The kind moves nothing itself: it draws where the row would land and announces `moved`, and the rows are the script's to reorder

sheet.description: The picture a `list` cuts its card faces from

close_on.description: What shuts a `menu`'s popup besides a row: a click outside it, any click at all, or nothing but Escape

options.description: The words a `menu` of strings offers, its `text` being the button's caption; `value_changed` carries every pick

placement.description: Where a `menu` opens: under its button, above it, to its right or to its left, each from the side's start (`below` starts at the button's left edge, `right` at its top) or at `_center` or `_end`; at the pointer; centred on the screen; or as a `sheet` along the screen's foot over a dim, as wide as the screen, which a `[narrow]` table asks for on a phone (daisyUI's `max-sm:modal-bottom`)

placement_fallbacks.description: The placements a `menu`'s popup tries, in order, where its own does not fit the screen; empty tries egui's, and naming the placement alone keeps it where it is

popup_gap.description: The space between a `menu`'s button and its popup, in design pixels; below zero takes egui's

popup_width.description: How wide a `menu`'s popup starts, in design pixels; 0 sizes it to its rows

showing.description: Holds a menu's rows up from the scene, as a click would; for an offscreen run or a tutorial, since nothing can click there

animate.description: Shimmer a `progress_bar` that is short of full, with a spinner at its end unless it states a `corner_radius`. It repaints every frame while it is on screen and short of full, and never otherwise

arrows.description: Draw a step up and a step down beside a `number_field`, each moving it by `step` within `min` and `max`

axis.description: Which way a `slider` runs: up its box under `vertical`, along it otherwise

clamp.description: Whether a `slider` holds its number inside `min` and `max`: `always`, one the scene set outside them included; `edits`, only what the reader enters; `never`, only the track

clamp_existing.description: Pull a `number_field`'s number back inside `min` and `max` where the scene set it outside them; off, it is shown as set and only an edit is bounded

decimals.description: How many decimals a `slider`'s or `number_field`'s number shows; below zero lets egui decide

drag_speed.description: How far a `number_field`, or a `slider`'s shown number, moves per design pixel dragged; 0 takes egui's, which is 1 on a number field and scales with the range on a slider

handle.description: A `slider`'s handle: a `circle`, or a `rect` `handle_aspect` times as wide as the track is tall

handle_aspect.description: How wide a `rect` handle is against its height

icon_color.description: A `number_field`'s prefix's ink, standing apart at its start, as `#rrggbb` or a name from the theme's `[colors]`, as an axis's letter in its axis colour; empty takes the role's `icon_color`

largest_finite.description: The largest number a `logarithmic` slider reaches short of an unbounded end; 0 is no limit

logarithmic.description: Space a `slider`'s track logarithmically, for a range across orders of magnitude

max.description: The high end of a `slider` or `progress_bar`; a `number_field` runs free while this pair is the default 0 and 1

min.description: The low end of a `slider` or `progress_bar`; a `number_field` runs free while this pair is the default 0 and 1

number_format.description: The base a `slider` or `number_field` writes its number in; the others than `decimal` write it whole

prefix.description: Text drawn before a `number_field`'s or a shown `slider`'s number with a space between

show_percentage.description: Draw a `progress_bar`'s fill as a percentage on it, in place of its `text`

show_value.description: Draw a `slider`'s number beside its track, for the reader to drag or type into

smallest_positive.description: The smallest number above zero a `logarithmic` slider reaches, for a range that starts at or crosses zero; 0 takes egui's millionth

smart_aim.description: Round a dragged `slider` to the simplest number near the pointer

step.description: The grid a `slider` snaps to, and how far a `number_field`'s `arrows` move it; 0 is continuous, and 1 for the arrows

suffix.description: Units drawn after a `number_field`'s or a shown `slider`'s number with a space between

trailing_fill.description: Fill a `slider`'s track from its start up to the handle

update_while_editing.description: Write a `slider`'s or `number_field`'s number as the reader types it; off, only once the typing is left

value.description: Where a `slider`, `number_field` or `progress_bar` stands, between `min` and `max`; a slider and a drag value write it and announce `value_changed` with it

items.description: The rows a `list`, `tree` or `table` holds. `text` is the key of the one picked, and every row event reports a row by its key

cells.description: A `table` row's text, one cell a column

depth.description: How many levels into a `tree` the row sits

icon.description: The name of a glyph in the theme's icon font, drawn before the label, and on a card over it

key.description: What `text`, `selection` and every row event know the row by, never drawn. Empty takes the label, or a `table` row's first cell, so two rows that say the same need one to stay two rows

label.description: What the row says, and on a card its caption

marks.description: Drawn at the right, the last rightmost, and reported by the `marked` event

icon.description: What it draws: the name of a glyph in the theme's icon font

name.description: What the `marked` event names when it is clicked

note.description: What the row trails at the right, and on a card its tooltip

region.description: On a card in a `list` that names a `sheet`, the part of that picture the card shows in place of its icon, as left, top, width and height in the picture's own pixels, as an `image`'s `region`; a zero width or height shows the icon

tint.description: The row's own `#rrggbb`; empty takes the widget's ink

multi_select.description: Let a `list`, `tree` or `table` hold more than one row: the platform's command key toggles a row and shift takes the run from the last one clicked

row_height.description: The pitch of a `list`, `tree` or `table` row, in design pixels; 0 takes the font's own line height

selection.description: The keys of the rows a `list`, `tree` or `table` has picked, one of them where it holds one. `text` is the key of the last row clicked, which is where a shift range measures from; `value_changed` carries the whole list where the widget holds many, and the key where it holds one

animated.description: Ease a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` to where it is sent, such as a row scrolled into view, rather than jump

axis.description: Which way a `scroll` moves, the other way its contents filling the box it was given; on a box whose `overflow` is `scroll`, which way it may be moved, its contents laid out as the box lays them out

drag_cursor.description: The pointer's shape while a drag scrolls a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table`'s content; `arrow` leaves it as it is

drag_scroll.description: When dragging a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table`'s content scrolls it: on a touch screen (or with `[input] emulate_touch_from_mouse`, the mouse standing in for a finger), always, or never; a `scroll_deadzone` takes the drag over itself, and a child that takes the drag itself (`sense = "drag"`, a slider) keeps it

min_scrolled_height.description: The shortest a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` draws while its content runs past it downwards, in design pixels; 0 takes egui's

min_scrolled_width.description: The narrowest a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` draws while its content runs past it sideways, in design pixels; 0 takes egui's

scroll_deadzone.description: How far a finger drags a `scroll` before it scrolls, in design pixels, so a tap on a child still lands; 0 takes the project's `[ui] scroll_deadzone`

scroll_offset.description: Where a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` is scrolled to, across and down, in design pixels: written as the reader scrolls, and a new one written by the scene or a script scrolls it there. Below zero on an axis leaves that axis where it is; `ui.scroll` takes it too

scrollbar.description: When a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` has its bars: while its content runs past it, always, or never. The bars float, so one shows once the pointer is over the box

stick_to_end.description: Keep a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table` at its end as content arrives, until the reader scrolls away from it; `ui.scroll` takes it too

wheel_scroll.description: Let the mouse wheel scroll a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table`

wheel_speed.description: How far a mouse wheel scrolls a `scroll`, `list`, `tree` or `table`, across and down, as a multiple of egui's own

axis.description: Which line a `separator` draws; `both` leaves it across its parent's direction

overhang.description: How far a `separator`'s line runs past each end of the room it was given, in design pixels; below zero stops it short

spacing.description: The room a `separator` takes across its line, in design pixels, the line drawn down its middle; below zero is 6

shortcut.description: A chord that clicks this widget wherever it is, as `cmd+shift+KeyS` or `F5`, spelled as `[input.actions]` spells one; a menu row fires while its menu is shut, and draws the chord against its far edge unless it says its own `trailing`

takes_typing.description: Whether `shortcut` takes its key ahead of a field being typed into, a plain key included, so the field never sees it: a completion list's arrows, Enter and Escape while it is up

while_typing.description: Whether `shortcut` fires while a text field holds the keyboard. A chord without cmd, ctrl or alt never does unless it is a function key, since that is typing; off, no chord does, for one the field has a use for itself, as `cmd+KeyZ`

header.description: Draw the strip that names a `table`'s columns. Off, its columns are still `titles`', and a table that names none keeps its first row as a row

reverse.description: Take a `table`'s rows the other way round: the `sort` descending, or the order they were given bottom to top where none is named

sort.description: The column the rows are ordered by, by the name in `titles`; empty leaves them in the order they were given. A cell that starts with a number sorts as one, so `12 KB` follows `3 KB`. `reverse` takes them the other way round

sortable.description: Let a click on the header sort by that column, and the next click on the same one turn it round; the column sorted by carries a caret

splitter_width.description: How wide a grab the seam between two of a `table`'s columns gets, in design pixels; 0 takes six

text_align.description: Where every cell of a `table` sits in its column; a column whose name ends in `>` pins its own to the right

titles.description: A `table`'s column names, in order, and with them how many columns it has: a name ending in `>` draws its column against the right edge, which is what a column of numbers wants. None takes the first row as the names

widths.description: Each column's share of the width, in the order `titles` names them: `["2", "1", "1"]` gives the first half and the other two a quarter each. Numbers and the text of them both; empty divides the width evenly, and a drag on a seam in the header writes the shares back

current_page.description: Which child a `tabs` shows, by node name; empty shows the first. A click on the strip writes it and announces `value_changed` with the page's name

line_break.description: Where a wrapped line may break

markup.description: Read inline marks in the text: `[b]`, `[i]`, `[color=#hex]`, `[center]`, `[right]`, `[wave amp=N freq=N]` and `[img=path width=N]`; off, brackets are text

max_lines.description: The most lines a wrapped label keeps; zero keeps every line

selectable.description: Let a drag over this label select its text, and the platform's copy key take it

show_tooltip_when_elided.description: Show a `label`'s whole text when the pointer rests on it and `truncate` cut it short

text_align.description: Where text sits in the width the widget was given

text_background.description: A wash behind the text of the kinds egui draws, a `checkbox`, `dropdown`, `menu`, `tabs`, `panel` and the like, where a `label` and a `button` shape their own; alpha 0 is none

truncate.description: Cut a caption too long for the width the widget was given and end it with an ellipsis; with neither this nor `wrap` a button clips it at its edge. A `dropdown` cuts its picked text

truncate_at.description: Which part of a cut caption the ellipsis stands in for

wrap.description: Break text to the width the widget was given instead of running past it on one line; a `dropdown` breaks its picked text

backdrop_color.description: What a `dialog` dims the screen behind it with, clear for no dim; unset (the default, a negative alpha) takes its theme's `backdrop`, else black at 55 %

collapsible.description: Give a `window`'s title bar an arrow that folds the window to its bar and back

dismissable.description: Let Escape or a click on the dim shut a `dialog`; off, only the scene does

hide_on_close.description: Whether a `window`'s close button shuts it; off, the button only emits `close_requested` and the script decides

open.description: Whether a `window` or `dialog` is up; shut, it draws nothing and keeps nothing out

resizable.description: Give a `window` a grip in its bottom-right corner that a drag resizes it by, writing `width` and `height` within `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width` and `max_height`

hooks: Once, when the script is attached and its scene has loaded.
Every frame, with the seconds since the last; not while a pause or the node's `process` mode holds it.
Every fixed step, with the step's length; not while a pause or the node's `process` mode holds it.
Once, as the node is freed or its script detached.
After the script's file changed and it was rebuilt, with its state kept.
The pointer came over the node.
A button went down over the node, then over every other node unless one answers `true`.
A button came up, reaching nodes as `on_pointer_down` does.
A press and release over the same node, or a click on its widget.
The pointer moved with a button held, having pressed on the node.
A drag ended over this node, from the node given.
A key went down; every node hears it, the last child first, until one answers `true`.
A key came up, reaching nodes as `on_key_down` does.
A declared input action was pressed, reaching nodes as `on_key_down` does.
A declared input action was let go, reaching nodes as `on_key_down` does.
The wheel turned, over the node or, over nothing, to every node.
The window's size, told to every node once the window first has one and whenever it changes.
A scene variable changed, told to every node at the end of the frame.
The node's `states` moved to another state.
The game paused or resumed, told to every script, a paused one too.
The window came to the front or left it, told to every script.
The system switched dark mode, told to every script.
The player turned the system's reduce-motion setting on or off, told to every script.
The window was asked to close; every script hears it, then the app goes.
The game went to the background or came back: a hidden tab, a minimised or covered window, an app sent back; told to every script.
The system is short of memory, on iOS and Android; told to every script.
The screen's safe area moved, as `[left, top, right, bottom]` in pixels; told to every script.
The screen turned, to `portrait` or `landscape`; told to every script.
A gamepad was plugged in, with the id `input` names it by; told to every script.
A gamepad went away, with its id; told to every script.
A pad's rumble ran its course, with the pad's id, the frame after; not sent for one stopped or replaced. Told to every script.
A script set a setting, `{ path, value }`; every script hears it the next frame.
The language changed; every script hears it the next frame.

modules.doc: Clip playback on a node's `animation` component: play, pause, seek and query. `tween` builds a short clip from a table of steps and returns a handle.

docs.add_clip: Give this node a clip of its own under that name, shaped like a scene file's.
docs.current_clip: The clip playing or paused on this node, and nil once it has ended, been stopped, or never started.
docs.current_state: The state the machine is in, or nil before it has entered one.
docs.ease: The curve `name` spells at `t`, from 0 to 1: what a tween's `ease` does to its progress, for a number a script moves itself. A name is an `EASE_*` constant or CSS's `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, solved as a browser solves it.
docs.ease_names: Every named curve an `ease` takes: the bare `linear`, then eleven transitions in four modes each. An `ease` takes CSS's `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` besides.
docs.is_playing: Whether a clip is advancing on this node; a paused, stopped, finished or absent one answers false.
docs.is_tween_running: Whether a handle still names a running tween; one that finished, was stopped, or lost its node answers false. Takes a tween handle, where `is_playing` takes a node and asks about its clip.
docs.jump: Cut the state machine to the named state on the next step, with no fade.
docs.pause: Hold the playhead where it is, keeping the clip current so `resume` has something to go back to.
docs.play: Start the clip of that name on this node; the trailing options table takes `speed_scale` (a multiplier), `from_start`, `blend_time` (seconds to blend out of the clip before), `ease` (the blend's curve, an `EASE_*` constant), and `retarget` (a `bone_map` reference, so this rig can play another rig's clips).
docs.queue: Play the clip of that name once the current one ends; a looping clip never ends, so a queue behind one never drains.
docs.resume: Carry on from where `pause` left off; a stopped, finished or never-started node is left alone.
docs.seek: Move the playhead to a number of seconds and pose the node there, even on a paused or ended clip.
docs.set_condition: Turn on or off a condition that `auto` transitions wait on.
docs.stop: End the clip on this node, leaving the pose where it is; `resume` cannot revive it.
docs.stop_tween: End the tween a handle names, leaving the pose where it is.
docs.time: Seconds of playback since the current clip started, before wrapping; a stopped clip keeps where it stopped.
docs.travel: Head for the named state through the cheapest chain of transitions, each costing its priority and fading as it says; a state no transition reaches is cut to directly.
docs.tween: Generate a clip on the node from a table of steps and run it, returning the handle `stop_tween` and `is_tween_running` take. The table also takes `delay` in seconds, `then = <handle>` to wait for another tween, `loops` and `speed_scale`; a step's `call` names a method; the node's `on_tween_finished(handle)` is called when it runs out.

modules.name: animation

modules.doc: Apple services beyond `platform.*`: Game Center `identity`, Sign in with Apple, Game Center's screens. Calls answer `task::wait` on a later tick as a map whose `kind` is an `EVENT_*` constant. What arrives unasked is the `apple_event` event, `events::listen(node, "apple_event")`: an invite, an iCloud change. A link that opened the game is `url_opened` on `platform_event`. Notifications are `platform.notify`, push `platform.register_for_push`, and purchases `platform.purchase` and the rest.

docs.access_point: Show or hide Game Center's floating access point, and answer whether it is showing.
docs.available: Whether this build has Apple's frameworks behind it.
docs.credential_state: Ask whether a saved Sign in with Apple account is still authorized, revoked, transferred or unknown, and return the id the answer carries.
docs.identity: Fetch the items a server needs to verify this Game Center player, and return the id the answer carries.
docs.listen_for_cloud_changes: Hear about another device changing the iCloud key-value store, as `cloud_changed` with the `reason` and the `keys` it touched.
docs.listen_for_invites: Hear about Game Center invites the player accepts, as `invite_accepted` with the sender's `player` id and `name`, and matches they ask for, as `match_requested` with the `players`.
docs.show_dashboard: Open Game Center's dashboard over the game, and return the id its `dashboard_closed` answer carries.
docs.sign_in: Sign in with Apple, and return the id the identity token comes back on. Game Center's own sign-in is `platform.sign_in`.

modules.name: apple

modules.doc: Asset definitions by reference: a project path, `file#entry` for one entry, `#id` for a scene block, or `id://<id>` from `assets/index.toml`. A script gets the definition table.

docs.directory: The project-relative directory files of an asset type belong in; empty when the type is unknown or declared none.
docs.exists: Whether a reference resolves to a definition that is really there; false rather than an error when it does not.
docs.invalidate: Declare everything derived from project files stale (a shader a material links, say) so it is rebuilt from disk; for a file the watcher does not cover. A script hears this and every reload with `events::listen(this.node, "assets_reloaded")`, as `on_assets_reloaded(generation)`.
docs.kind_of: Which importer kind a file is by its extension — `texture`, `audio`, `font` or `model` — or empty for one none claims. A `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.ttc` or `.fnt` is a font.
docs.load: The definition table behind a reference, from the cache: the script's own copy, so editing it disturbs no other holder. An error when the reference resolves to nothing; `reload` first for a fresh read of the file.
docs.reload: Forget a reference so the next load re-reads its file, along with every entry cut from that same file.
docs.rename: Move a file or directory and rewrite every reference to it in the project's `.toml` files, comments kept; answers the files rewritten. Paths as `fs.*` takes them, so an editor refactors the game it has open by absolute path. Script sources are not rewritten: a path in a `.bs` is the script's own value, and `id://` is the reference that survives a move.
docs.save: Write a definition table to the project-relative file a reference names; an error unless it names a whole file.
docs.schema: The properties a record asset type holds, in the order it writes them; nil for a type that is not a record.

modules.name: assets

modules.doc: Sound playback: `play` starts a node's `sound` component and returns a handle that `is_playing` takes; `seek` and `skip` move it, and the node's `sound` properties change it as it plays. `play_file` plays a file on a node of its own, from a `position` heard from the `listener` when given one. A node's `sound` announces `sound_finished` (`EVENT_SOUND_FINISHED`) with the handle when it plays out. `devices` lists the outputs `[audio] device` can name.

docs.bus_effects: One bus's effects as `[audio.buses]` declares them, applied once to everything the bus mixes. Built when the output device opens, as the limiter is. Nil for a bus with none switched on.
docs.bus_limit: One bus's limiter as `[audio.buses]` declares it. Nil for a bus with none.
docs.bus_volume_linear: One bus's own gain, without its parents'.
docs.buses: Every audio bus, declared in `[audio.buses]` or made by setting a volume, in name order.
docs.device_ready: Whether an output device is open. False on a page until the first gesture, and false for good with no sound card; playing before then hands out handles that make no sound. Recorded: a replay answers what its recording did, whatever the machine it runs on has.
docs.devices: Every output device's name, as `[audio] device` takes it. Empty when the platform lists none. Recorded, as `device_ready` is.
docs.distance_gain: The gain the distance to the listener is costing a positional handle right now: 1 up close, 0 out of range.
docs.emitter_position: Where a handle played with a `position` is; nil for a flat or unknown one.
docs.is_playing: Whether a handle's sound is still going: false once it plays out or is stopped, on the same tick with or without an output device.
docs.listener_position: Where the ears are: the current `listener` node's world position, else the current camera's.
docs.pan: Where a positional handle sits between the speakers: -1 hard left, 0 centred, 1 hard right.
docs.play: Start the node's own `sound` from the top, replacing what it had going, and return the new handle.
docs.play_file: Play a sound file on a node of its own under the scene's root, through `bus` at `volume_linear` and `pitch_scale`, looping when `loop` is true; a `position` places it, heard from the `listener` over `min_distance` to `max_distance`. Returns the node, which frees itself once the sound plays out: free it to stop the sound, or set its `sound` to change it.
docs.seek: Jump the node's sound to `seconds` into the file it is playing; `playback_time` reads it back. A node with nothing playing is left alone.
docs.set_bus_volume_linear: Set one bus's gain and re-apply it to everything already playing on it: which is what a volume slider is.
docs.set_emitter_position: Move what a handle plays from, so a sound follows something the script is driving; the frame takes its doppler from how far it moved.
docs.skip: Move the node's sound on to the next file in its `queue`. Past the last one it has played out, and the node announces `sound_finished`.
docs.stop: Silence what the node's `sound` started, over its `fade_out_time`; a node carrying none is left alone.
docs.stop_all: Silence everything at once and clear the playback every `sound` component was holding.

modules.name: audio

modules.doc: The page a browser build runs in; off the web every query answers nil. A parent-frame message is the `browser_event` event: `events::listen(node, "browser_event")`, heard as `on_browser_event(payload)`.

docs.hardware_concurrency: How many threads the browser reports, or nil off the web.
docs.location: The page's URL as it loaded, or nil off the web.
docs.post_message: Post a value to the page that embeds this one. False off the web, and false while a recording plays.
docs.replace_location: Put `path` in the page's address without loading it, as the web's `history.replaceState`, so a refresh opens it again: what an app keeps its page in. False off the web, and false while a recording plays.
docs.user_agent: The browser's user agent string, or nil off the web.
docs.visible: Whether the tab is in front of the player; true off the web.

modules.name: browser

modules.doc: Breakpoints, pausing a script and resuming it. The editor's Debugger dock and the Debug Adapter Protocol server drive the same machinery. The editor has this module; a game's runtime does not.

docs.break_on_error: Whether a script that throws stops rather than being logged.
docs.breakpoints: The lines one file's breakpoints landed on.
docs.request_break: Ask to stop at the next line any script runs; nothing is stopped yet when it returns.
docs.resume: Let the stopped script go on, in the given step mode (`CONTINUE`, `STEP_OVER`, `STEP_INTO`, `STEP_OUT`).
docs.scope: The node whose subtree a pause holds still, or nil when a pause stops the whole tree.
docs.set_break_on_error: Stop where a script throws instead of logging it and moving on; off by default.
docs.set_breakpoints: Replace one file's breakpoints with the given lines, returning the lines they landed on.
docs.set_scope: Limit the pause to one node's subtree, so an editor keeps running while the game stops; nil means the whole tree.
docs.stop_location: Where a script is stopped, or nil while none is. A script hears a stop with `events::listen(this.node, "debugger_stopped")`, as `on_debugger_stopped(stop)`, and the script going on as `debugger_resumed`, rather than asking every frame.

modules.name: debugger

modules.doc: The projects a game imports whole under `deps/<alias>/`, declared in `[dependencies]`. An installed dependency is read-only: `fs.*` and `assets.save` refuse to write into one. A relative path a dependency's script builds reads from that dependency's own folder. Every runtime has `list` and `of`; the verbs that write a project are the editor's.

docs.add_path: Declare `alias = { path = "<path>" }` in a game's `[dependencies]`, comments kept, and install it. An empty game is the open project.
docs.install: Read a game's `[dependencies]` again and install each: what a dependency fetched while the editor runs needs to become a root. An empty game is the open project.
docs.list: Every installed dependency: its alias, where it sits, where it came from and its licence.
docs.make_local: Copy a dependency's file into the game and point the game's references at the copy; answers the game's files rewritten. The copy never updates. A document's own paths come out as the game names the dependency's files.
docs.move_into: Move game files into a `path` dependency, each at the same place under its root, and point the game's references at `deps/<alias>/…`; answers the files rewritten.
docs.of: The alias of the dependency a path lies in, or nil for one of the game's own.

modules.name: dependency

modules.doc: What a phone lends a game beyond the store: its motor, the share sheet, the photo picker and the store's review prompt. A call that answers does so through `task::wait` with a map whose `kind` is `shared`, `picked`, `done`, `cancelled`, `error` or `unsupported`, each an `EVENT_*` constant. `platform::is_available` says which of them work here. A test answers `share`, `pick_photo` and `request_review` from the file `BALAUR_STAND_INS` names.

docs.haptic: One tap of feedback, named by a `HAPTIC_*` constant: iOS's feedback generators, Android's predefined effects, a short buzz on a page. Nothing on a desktop, and never recorded.
docs.pick_photo: Show the OS's picker of one picture over the game, and return the id its answer carries: `picked` with the file's `bytes` (`[int]`) and its media `type` (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`), `cancelled` when shut with none, `error`, or `unsupported` where there is no picker. iOS's photo picker answers a JPEG; Android's photo picker, a Mac's, Windows' or Linux's file dialog (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP) and a page's file input the file as it is. `image::encode_async` makes it small enough to upload.
docs.request_review: Ask the store to show its prompt to rate the game, and return the id its `done` answer carries. The store decides whether it shows, and says nothing about what the player did. On Android it is Play's review flow, in a build whose `[android] capabilities` has `in-app-review`; `unsupported` anywhere else.
docs.share: Show the OS's share sheet over the game, and return the id its answer carries: `shared` with the `target` the player picked where the OS names it, `cancelled`, `error`, or `unsupported` where there is no sheet.
docs.vibrate: Buzz the device's motor for that many seconds: Android's vibrator, a page's `navigator.vibrate`, the iPhone's one system buzz whatever the length. Nothing on a desktop, and never recorded, like rumble.

modules.name: device

modules.doc: Bytes to base64 text and back, and UTF-8 bytes back to text.

docs.base64: Bytes as standard base64 with padding; a value outside 0 to 255 traps.
docs.from_base64: The bytes a base64 string encodes, in the standard alphabet with its padding; text that is not base64 traps.
docs.from_utf8: The text UTF-8 bytes spell; nil when they are not UTF-8, a value outside 0 to 255 included.

modules.name: encoding

modules.doc: The running app: its clock, command-line `args`, `user_data_dir`, loaded `plugins` and `quit`.

docs.args: The command-line arguments the app was started with, empty when it was given none.
docs.dark_mode: Whether the system is in dark mode this tick; every script's `on_dark_mode_changed(bool)` is called when it changes. False where nothing says.
docs.delta: Seconds the frame in progress covers, the same number a system is handed.
docs.device_id: One id per install, made on first use and kept in the user directory: what a device login sends. Recorded with the session.
docs.environment: An environment variable's value, nil when it is unset. Nil on the web, which has none. Outside the simulation, like `args`: a replay does not record it.
docs.focused: Whether the window is in front of the player this tick; every script's `on_focused_changed(bool)` is called when it changes. True with no window.
docs.function_costs: What each function has cost since `set_script_profiling(true)`, dearest first: a list of `{ function, calls, instructions }`, a function's own statements without its callees'. A function of a module two files use counts once for the two.
docs.open_url: Open an http, https or mailto URL in whatever the player browses with: an opener on a desktop, a new tab on the web, the browser on a phone. An effect on the world outside the game: never recorded, and it does nothing while a recording plays.
docs.plugin_version: The version of one loaded plugin, or nil when it did not load: how a game shipped without `http` says so rather than call into a module that is not there.
docs.plugins: Every plugin this build loaded, named, in load order.
docs.prefers_reduced_motion: Whether the player asked the system to reduce motion this tick, as CSS's `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: macOS's and iOS's Reduce Motion, Android's Remove animations, Windows' Show animations off, GNOME's animations off, a browser's media query. Every script's `on_prefers_reduced_motion_changed(bool)` is called when it changes. False where nothing says; a test names it in the file `BALAUR_STAND_INS` names, `"engine.prefers_reduced_motion": "reduce"` or `"no-preference"`.
docs.quit: Ask the app to shut down; the frame in flight still finishes, and the process exits with `code`, 0 when left out.
docs.reload_scripts: Recompile scripts by their project-relative keys in one build, however many there are, for a tool editing files outside the watched root; answers what kept them from compiling, empty when they did.
docs.reveal: Show a file or directory in the system file manager, selected where the platform can. Desktops only: neither a browser tab nor a phone has a file manager to ask. Never recorded, like `open_url`.
docs.script_costs: What each script has cost since `set_script_profiling(true)`, dearest first: a list of `{ path, calls, instructions }`, `calls` the engine's calls into it. A file counts the statements it ran: not seconds, so the number is the same on every machine.
docs.set_content_root: Play the content of the project at `root`: its `strings/` catalogues and its `fonts/` are read from there, and the subtree `debugger.set_scope` names draws in them. For a host running a project other than its own: the editor, whose own root has neither. An empty string plays the project's own again.
docs.set_paused: Pause or resume the game. Every node whose `process` mode is `pausable` stops ticking, physics holds both worlds, and the frame loop keeps drawing; an `always` subtree is what a pause menu runs in. Every script's `on_paused_changed(bool)` follows, the ones the pause just stopped included.
docs.set_script_profiling: Start or stop counting what each script costs. Turning it on clears the tally; on from off, or off from on, rebuilds every Balaur Script file between frames, with counters or without, carrying its fields across.
docs.set_time_scale: Multiply wall-clock time before the simulation is owed it: 0.5 is slow motion, 2.0 fast forward, each still whole fixed steps. Zero stops time without stopping a single node. A replay and a networked session drive by tick and ignore it.
docs.target: Where this runs: `{ os, web, mobile, touchscreen, editor, dev }`, `dev` being a run from the sources rather than an exported pack. Recorded in a session's header, so a replay on another machine answers as the original did.
docs.tick: Which frame this is, counted whole: what simulation code branches on instead of `time`.
docs.tick_hz: How many fixed steps a second this run takes, from `[time] tick_hz`. 60 unless the project says otherwise.
docs.time: Seconds of engine time since the app started, accumulated as a float.
docs.time_scale: What time is being multiplied by; 1.0 is real time.
docs.time_zone: The player's time zone by its IANA name, as `Europe/Madrid`: what a server that keeps a zone by name is sent. macOS's and iOS's system zone, Android's setting, Windows' zone as CLDR names it, a Linux's `TZ` or `/etc/localtime`, a page's `Intl` zone. Nil where the platform names none. Read from the system on each call, never recorded, and no hook says it changed: read it when it is needed. A test names it in the file `BALAUR_STAND_INS` names, `"engine.time_zone": "Europe/Madrid"`.
docs.timings: What the last frame cost, in seconds: `{ frame, fixed_steps, stages, spans }`. Presentation only: branching a `fixed_update` on wall time desyncs, and nothing records it.
docs.unix_time: The wall clock at the top of this tick, in seconds since 1970. Read once per frame and recorded, so a replay sees the time the recording saw. A tool's own script, on a node outside the subtree `debugger::set_scope` names, reads the machine's clock, which a replay does not feed.
docs.user_data_directory: A writable per-user directory for saves and settings, created on first call and named after the project. A game the editor plays answers with its own, the folder it has when run alone.
docs.user_data_directory_of: The user data directory a project of that name has, not created: where a tool finds another game's saves and logs.
docs.utc_offset: How far the player's time zone is from UTC at `at` (seconds since 1970), in seconds east, daylight saving included: `unix_time() + utc_offset(t)` is what their clock says of `t`. 0 where the platform says nothing. Read from the system, never recorded.
docs.watch: Follow a directory outside the project the way a run follows the project: a script loaded from it hot reloads when its file changes, and with no `extensions` every other file reloads as the project's own content does. A script hears each burst of changes once with `events::listen(this.node, "files_changed")`, as `on_files_changed(paths)`, each path spelled from `directory` and with one of `extensions`, or any file when that is empty. A run hears its own project's files the same way, by project-relative path, every file but its scripts and those under a dot folder. An empty list is more than the watcher could name, so what is held has to be checked again. Answers false where nothing can be followed: a pack, a browser, a run with watching off, as `balaur run --headless` and `--offscreen` are without `--watch`. The directory has to be one `fs` may reach.

modules.name: engine

modules.doc: Named events between scripts. A node hears its own events, and after `listen` another node's, as its `on_<name>(payload, source)` method; `node.emit` and `events.emit` send one.

docs.emit: Queue an event from no particular node, delivered at the top of the next frame's update to whoever listens for the name from anyone.
docs.listen: Hear an event on this node, as its script's `on_<name>(payload, source)`, `source` being the node that said it, or nil for one said from no node. Pass the node whose events to hear, or leave it out for every emitter. Listening twice is once.
docs.next: A token for `task.wait` that wakes, with the payload, the next time the name is delivered from that node or, left out, from anyone: `let payload = task::wait(events::next("finished", door)).await;`, a GDScript `await door.finished`.
docs.stop_listening: Stop hearing an event on this node, `from` being the emitter it listened with. Not an error when it never listened.

modules.name: events

modules.doc: Exports the project being edited. `targets` lists what this install can build; `start` runs one off the frame and reports as the `export_event` event: `events::listen(node, "export_event")`, heard as `on_export_event`, as each export starts, finishes or fails.

docs.output: Where an export for this target will be written, as the project's `[export] output` decides.
docs.preview: What one file becomes in a target's pack, as the Import tab shows it: `{ source, before, after, width, height, drawn_width, drawn_height, gpu_bytes }`, where `source` is the file or the variant that ships and `drawn_*` is zero unless a smaller copy does. Nil when the file does not ship there. An empty target is this machine's own.
docs.running_count: How many exports are in flight.
docs.start: Export the edited project for one target, on a thread. `download` allows fetching a missing template, `sign` names an identity, `output` overrides where it lands. Answers false while a recording plays.
docs.targets: Every target, each `{ name, runtime, bundle, installed, fetchable, note }`: the runtime the project's `[export] runtime` puts it on, whether that is already here, whether a missing one could be fetched, and what a signed build of it would also need.

modules.name: export

modules.doc: Projects kept on Forge, for the editor's pickers, and adding one to a game as a dependency. `balaur add` and `balaur fetch` are the same code. `BALAUR_FORGE` names the Forge and `BALAUR_FORGE_TOKEN` reads private projects.

docs.add: Add `owner/name` to the game's `[dependencies]` and fetch it into `deps/<alias>/`, on a thread. `forge_event` hears `{ kind: "fetched", alias }` or `failed` with `job: "add"`.
docs.copy: Copy `owner/name` at its default branch into a new folder under `parent`, with its dependencies fetched, on a thread: the project manager's Open a copy. `forge_event` hears `{ kind: "copied", path }` or `failed` with `job: "copy"`.
docs.fetch: Fill the game's `deps/` from `project.lock`, or with `update` move each dependency to its newest commit, on a thread. `forge_event` hears `{ kind: "fetched", alias: "" }` or `failed` with `job: "fetch"`.
docs.search: List public projects on a thread, either filter empty for none. `forge_event` hears `{ kind: "listed", rows }`, each `{ project, description, tags, license }` with `project` as `owner/name`, or `{ kind: "failed", job: "search", message }`. False while a recording plays.
docs.url: The Forge this machine asks, without a trailing slash.

modules.name: forge

modules.doc: Files on disk, project-relative unless the path is absolute. In a packed build `read`, `exists` and `list` reach what the pack holds.

docs.copy: Copy a file byte for byte, creating the destination's parent first. What `read` and `write` cannot do for an image or a model.
docs.create_directory: Create a project-relative directory and every parent it needs.
docs.exists: Whether a project-relative path has anything at it, file or directory.
docs.list: A directory's entries as `{ name, is_dir }`, sorted, dotfiles skipped; empty for a directory that is not there.
docs.modified_time: When a file last changed, in seconds since the Unix epoch; nil for one that is not there.
docs.read: A whole file as text, project-relative unless absolute and found inside the pack in a packed run; nil when it cannot be read.
docs.remove: Delete a project-relative file, or a directory and everything under it; false when there was nothing there.
docs.rename: Move a project-relative file or directory, creating the destination's parent first.
docs.size: How many bytes a file holds, as a cache's "free up space" counts them; nil for one that is not there and for a directory.
docs.write: Write text to a project-relative file, creating the directory it goes in. The text lands in a file beside it, synced, then renamed over it, so a crash mid-write keeps the old file whole.

modules.name: fs

modules.doc: Polygons on the plane as lists of `Vec2` points in outline order: triangulation, booleans, hulls and containment. Every answer is identical on every platform.

docs.area: The polygon's area, always positive whatever its winding.
docs.contains: Whether a point lies inside the polygon. A point exactly on an edge may answer either way.
docs.convex_decomposition: The polygon cut into convex pieces that overlap across their seams, so nothing wedges into one; `overlap` from 0 to 1 says how far each piece grows, 0.9 by default.
docs.convex_hull: The smallest convex polygon around the points, counter-clockwise.
docs.difference: Everything inside the first polygon and outside the second, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.fill: The polygon filled however its outline runs, crossing itself included: the points the fill needed, the polygon's as given and one at each place it crosses itself, and counter-clockwise `[i, j, k]` triangles over them; a polygon with no area has none.
docs.intersection: Everything inside both polygons, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.is_clockwise: Whether the points run clockwise, with y up.
docs.segments_intersect: Where two segments cross, or nil when they do not; touching at an endpoint counts.
docs.symmetric_difference: Everything inside exactly one of the two polygons, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.triangulate: The polygon cut into triangles, as `[i, j, k]` triples indexing its points, counter-clockwise; either winding is accepted. A polygon that crosses itself is refused, since filling it needs a vertex at each crossing: `fill` answers those too.
docs.union: Everything inside either polygon: a list of shapes, each a list of paths whose first is the outline and the rest holes. `opts` takes `fill_rule` (`even_odd`, `non_zero`, `positive`, `negative`; `even_odd` unless given), `min_area`, `keep_collinear` and `clean_result`, as `boolean2d` does.

modules.name: geometry2d

modules.doc: Mesh operations: hulls, convex decomposition, voxelisation, cutting and boolean intersection, on a `Mesh` that `load_mesh` reads from an asset or a script builds.

docs.convex_decomposition: The mesh cut into convex pieces, each one a mesh: the only way to collide a concave shape dynamically.
docs.convex_hull: The tightest convex shape containing every point: what a dynamic collider wants when the model is concave.
docs.intersect: The mesh both meshes have in common, or nothing when they do not overlap.
docs.pieces: The mesh's separate parts, one mesh each: what a model that was already broken is made of.
docs.split: Cut the mesh with a plane, returning the two halves, nil for a half with nothing in it.
docs.voxelize: The mesh as a voxel grid (`size` and `cells`, ready to be a `voxels` asset) so a model can become destructible terrain.

modules.name: geometry3d

modules.doc: Google services: Sign in with Google on Android 14 and later, through the system's Credential Manager. A call answers `task::wait` on a later tick as a map whose `kind` is an `EVENT_*` constant.

docs.sign_in: Sign in with Google, and return the id the answer carries: `signed_in` with `token` (an id token for `[google] server_client_id`), `email` and `name`; `cancelled`; `unsupported` off Android, below Android 14, with no client id or with no Google account on the device; or `error`. The accounts already signed in to the app come first, without a tap when there is one.

modules.name: google

modules.doc: SHA-256 content hashes of files and strings.

docs.sha256_file: The SHA-256 of a file as lowercase hex, read through the project's file roots; an absolute path is read as given.
docs.sha256_text: The SHA-256 of a string as lowercase hex.

modules.name: hash

modules.doc: HTTP requests off the frame: `method`, `headers`, `body` or `body_bytes`, `timeout_seconds` and `save_to` options. `task::wait` on the id answers a map whose `kind` is `response`, with `status`, `headers` and `body`, or `error`; a `save_to` download reports as the `http_progress` event with `kind` `progress`, and a body over 256 KB going out with `kind` `upload`, natively; a browser's fetch does not report one. Each kind is an `EVENT_*` constant.

docs.cancel: Stop waiting on a request: its reply is dropped, a download stops writing, and any await hears `kind` `cancelled` next frame. False when it had already finished.
docs.in_flight: How many requests started here have an answer, `cancelled` included, still to be delivered; 0 means every one has woken its waiter, so a test's end waits with `while http::in_flight() > 0 { await task::frames(1); }`.
docs.request: Start an HTTP request and return the id `task::wait` answers its reply on. With `save_to` the body is written under the user directory and the reply says where in `path`.

modules.name: http

modules.doc: A picture's bytes, PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or BMP, decoded, turned upright as its EXIF orientation says, fitted inside `max_side_pixels` and written again: what a photo from `device::pick_photo` goes through before an upload. `encode_async` does the work off the frame.

docs.encode: The picture `bytes` hold, written as `opts` asks, or nil where they are no picture this reads. A photo takes tens of milliseconds: call `encode_async` from a frame that has to stay smooth.
docs.encode_async: `encode` on a worker: the id `task::wait` answers the bytes on, or nil, once it is done.

modules.name: image

modules.doc: Imports a `.glb` or `.gltf` model, an `.aseprite` sprite, or a `.tmx` or `.ldtk` level into the project being edited, with the importers `balaur import` runs.

docs.cancel: Stop the imports in flight at the end of the file each is writing. What they had written stays where it landed; each reports `cancelled` with the count it reached.
docs.choose: Ask the reader for a file and import what they pick, reporting as `start` does. On a desktop that is the OS dialog; in a tab it is the page's own chooser, which takes several files at once so a `.gltf` can be picked with the images it names. Answers whether the asking began.
docs.file: Import one file into the edited project, in one call. A whole project is the work of seconds, so an editor keeping its frame wants `start`.
docs.handles: Whether an importer claims this file, by extension.
docs.running_count: How many imports are in flight.
docs.start: Import one file into the edited project, or into `project` when one is named, a few files per frame, each reported as the `import_event` event: `events::listen(node, "import_event")`, heard as `on_import_event`, as an import starts, writes each file, finishes or fails. Answers false while a recording plays. A model and a sprite are read first and then written a slice at a time; a level walks its own folder and takes one long slice, which says so in `files`.

modules.name: import

modules.doc: One frame of input: keyboard, mouse, touch screen and gamepads, plus what went down or came up this frame. A headless run answers every query neutrally.

docs.action_down: Whether the action is held down now.
docs.action_just_pressed: Whether the action went down this frame.
docs.action_just_released: Whether the action came up this frame.
docs.action_value: How far the action is pushed, -1 to 1; a key answers 0 or 1, a stick or `keys:KeyA,KeyD` the whole range.
docs.actions: Every action `[input.actions]` declares, so a rebinding screen can list them.
docs.bind: Rebind the action to a list of bindings, spelled as `[input.actions]` spells them, replacing what it had and saving to the user data directory.
docs.bindings: What the action is bound to now, whether from the project or from the player's own rebinding.
docs.composing: The text an input method is still composing, for a field to show under its caret; empty once it commits into `typed`, and always empty without an input method.
docs.gamepad_acceleration: The pad's acceleration in g, gravity included, so a pad at rest reads 1 on one axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no accelerometer.
docs.gamepad_axis: How far the pad's `GAMEPAD_AXIS_*` stick or trigger is pushed: a stick -1 to 1 with up and right positive, a trigger 0 to 1, after `[input] gamepad_deadzone`; zero at rest and for an absent pad.
docs.gamepad_can_rumble: Whether the pad has motors to rumble; false for a pad that is not connected.
docs.gamepad_down: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button is held down: pressed past `[input] gamepad_press`, and not yet back under `gamepad_release`.
docs.gamepad_gyro: How fast the pad is turning, in radians per second about each axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no gyroscope.
docs.gamepad_info: Who the pad is; nil for an absent pad.
docs.gamepad_just_pressed: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button went down this frame; a press and a release between two frames are both seen.
docs.gamepad_just_released: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.gamepad_name: The pad's name: its mapping's when one matched, else the platform's. Empty when no pad has that id.
docs.gamepad_power: The pad's power. Read whenever the pad sends anything.
docs.gamepad_pressure: How far the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button is pressed, 0 to 1, before any deadzone: a digital button reads 0 or 1, a trigger or a pressure-sensitive button anything between.
docs.gamepad_repeated: True the frame the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button goes down, then every `[input] gamepad_repeat_interval_seconds` once it has been held for `gamepad_repeat_delay_seconds`: for stepping through a menu.
docs.gamepad_rumble: Rumble the pad. Options: `strong` and `weak`, the two motors at 0..1; `duration` in seconds; `delay` before it starts; `pulse` and `gap` to beat on and off; `attack`, `attack_level`, `fade` and `fade_level` to shape each pulse; `position` with `min_distance`, `max_distance`, `falloff` (`inverse`, `linear` or `exponential`) and `rolloff` to weaken it with distance from `gamepad_set_listener`. Returns whether the pad can rumble; a second rumble replaces the first.
docs.gamepad_set_listener: Where the pad's player is, for a rumble given a `position`; until set, a placed rumble plays at full strength.
docs.gamepad_stop_rumble: Silence the pad now, without the `on_gamepad_rumble_finished` a rumble's natural end sends.
docs.gamepad_touches: Every finger on the pad's touchpad, oldest first, with x and y running 0 to 1 across the surface. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; empty for a pad with no touchpad.
docs.gamepads: The ids of every connected pad: player slots from 0. A pad takes the lowest free slot last held by the same model, else the lowest free slot, and keeps it while connected.
docs.key_down: Whether the `KEY_*` key is held down right now, however many frames it has been down. `KEY_SHIFT`, `KEY_CONTROL`, `KEY_ALT` and `KEY_META` answer for either side.
docs.key_just_pressed: Whether the `KEY_*` key went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.key_just_released: Whether the `KEY_*` key came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.keyboard_height: How much of the window the on-screen keyboard covers, in pixels from the bottom: what a form moves up by. Zero with no keyboard up, and always zero on a desktop.
docs.long_press: Where a finger has been held still past `long_press_seconds`. Reported once per finger, on the frame the hold passes; nil otherwise.
docs.mouse_delta: How far the cursor moved this frame, in pixels; movement, not a position.
docs.mouse_down: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button is held down right now, however many frames it has been down.
docs.mouse_just_pressed: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_just_released: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_position: The cursor's position in window pixels, with (0, 0) at the top-left corner. A script hears it move with `events::listen(this.node, "pointer_moved")`, as `on_pointer_moved([x, y])`, and a button go down or up anywhere, the UI included, as `pointer_pressed` and `pointer_released` with `{ button, x, y }`; the wheel turn as `pointer_scrolled` with `[x, y]`, and two fingers as `pointer_gestured` with `{ scale, x, y, pan_x, pan_y }`.
docs.pan: Two or more fingers moving together: the average movement since last frame, in the same pixels as `mouse_position`. Zero with fewer than two down.
docs.pinch: Two fingers moving apart or together as `{ scale, center }`: `scale` above 1 is apart, measured against last frame, and `center` is the point between them. Empty with fewer than two fingers down.
docs.reset_bindings: Drop every saved rebinding and go back to what the project declared.
docs.scroll_delta: How far the wheel turned this frame, as an (x, y) pair; zero when it did not turn.
docs.set_action_value: Put a value into an action for one frame without a binding, the way a `touch_button` does; the furthest from rest wins where something else feeds the same action. Takes effect on the next tick, since actions derive at the top of one.
docs.set_gamepad: Report a pad as if a backend had, from next frame. A pad fed anything connects; `connected: false` unplugs it.
docs.set_key_down: Press or release a `KEY_*` key as if the window had reported it: next frame's edge, and the state until the opposite call.
docs.set_mouse_down: Press or release a `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button as if the window had reported it, from next frame; the widget under the cursor answers it in that frame's UI pass.
docs.set_mouse_position: Move the cursor to a window-pixel position as if the window had reported it, from next frame; the delta accumulates for that frame, and widgets answer it in that frame's UI pass.
docs.set_scroll_delta: Turn the wheel as if the window had reported it, from next frame; adds to that frame's `scroll_delta`, and a `scroll` under the cursor moves in that frame's UI pass.
docs.set_touch: Put a finger on the screen as if the window had reported it: `phase` is `start`, `move`, `end` or `cancel`, and the position is in the same pixels as `mouse_position`. Widgets answer it in the next frame's UI pass as they do a real finger: the first one down drives the pointer, so it presses, drags and long-presses.
docs.swipe: A finger that travelled far enough before it lifted. Reported on the frame it lifted and never again; nil otherwise.
docs.touches: Every finger on the screen, oldest first, in the same pixels as `mouse_position`.
docs.touches_just_ended: The ids of the fingers that lifted or were cancelled this frame.
docs.touches_just_started: The ids of the fingers that touched down this frame.
docs.typed: The characters typed this frame, in order: what a text field appends, where `key_just_pressed` says which key went down.

modules.name: input

modules.doc: JSON text to and from script values. Its `null` keeps nil through a round trip.

docs.encode: A value written back out as JSON text; NaN, infinity, a node or a callback has no JSON form and is an error.
docs.parse: The value a JSON document describes; nil for text that does not parse, as for `null`.
docs.parse_async: `parse` off the frame: the text is parsed on a worker, and `task::wait` on the token answers its value on the first tick after it is done; a replay wakes it on the tick the recording did, a rollback session on the next tick: `let pack = await task::wait(json::parse_async(text));`.

modules.name: json

modules.doc: The `info`, `warn` and `error` levels a script writes at, and the buffer behind them. Lines go through the engine's own `tracing` stream.

docs.clear: Empty the buffer, so a console reading it starts again from nothing.
docs.error: Write a line at error level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.file: The file this run's log is written to, or nil when it keeps none. `[log] file` turns it off and `[log] keep` says how many past runs stay beside it.
docs.info: Write a line at info level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.print: Write a line to standard output as it stands, with no level or tag and not into the buffer: what a headless run prints for a tool to read.
docs.since: What was logged after `cursor` (a `seq`, 0 for all the buffer holds), as `{ entries, cursor, missed }`: pass `cursor` back next time, and `missed` counts lines the buffer dropped before they were read. A script hears that there is more with `events::listen(this.node, "logged")`, as `on_logged(total)`, rather than asking every frame.
docs.warn: Write a line at warning level, tagged as coming from a script.

modules.name: log

modules.doc: Deterministic float maths backed by pure-Rust `libm`: the same inputs give the same bits on every platform.

docs.abs: The magnitude, with the sign dropped.
docs.acos: The angle in radians whose cosine is the argument, from 0 to PI; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.asin: The angle in radians whose sine is the argument, from -PI/2 to PI/2; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.atan: The angle in radians whose tangent is the argument, from -PI/2 to PI/2.
docs.atan2: The angle in radians from the positive x axis to the point, taking y first and x second.
docs.ceil: The smallest whole number at or above the argument, still a float.
docs.clamp: The first argument held inside the range given by the second (low) and third (high).
docs.cos: The cosine of an angle in radians.
docs.exp: e raised to the given power.
docs.floor: The largest whole number at or below the argument, still a float.
docs.log: The natural logarithm; -INF at zero and NaN below it.
docs.log10: The base-10 logarithm; -INF at zero and NaN below it.
docs.pow: The first argument raised to the power of the second.
docs.round: The nearest whole number, with halfway cases going away from zero.
docs.sin: The sine of an angle in radians.
docs.sqrt: The square root; NaN for a negative argument.
docs.tan: The tangent of an angle in radians.

modules.name: math

modules.doc: Thousands of copies of one sprite in one draw, each with its own transform, colour and custom data, through `node.multimesh2d`.

docs.instance_color: The colour one instance draws in.
docs.instance_count: How many instances the node holds.
docs.instance_custom_data: One instance's four floats of custom data, as a colour.

docs.set_visible_instance_count: How many instances draw, from the first; -1 draws them all.

modules.doc: Host, join and play a rollback match. Set this machine's input with `set_input` and read every slot's with `rollback.input(slot)`; events are the `multiplayer_event` event: `events::listen(node, "multiplayer_event")`, heard as `on_multiplayer_event`, a map with a `kind`.

docs.add_bot: On a host, a slot its own script plays with `set_input_for`; answers the slot, or nil when the lobby is full.
docs.host: Listen and take slot 0; answers `{ url, cert_hash, transport }`, what a joiner needs. Options over `[multiplayer]`: `transport`, `address`, `players`, `scene`, `depth`, `timeout_seconds`, `name`, `token`.
docs.join: Dial a host at a `ws://` or `https://` url; `connected` or `failed` follows. Options: `cert_hash` for a self-signed host, `name`, `token`, `timeout_seconds`.
docs.leave: Say goodbye and go idle; a host leaving ends the match for everyone.
docs.local_player: This machine's own slot, or nil before it has one.
docs.players: Every slot as `{ slot, name, bot, local, status }`, `status` as of the tick being simulated.
docs.set_input: What this machine's player does on the next tick, until set again; ignored while a tick re-runs.
docs.set_input_for: The same for a bot slot this machine plays.
docs.settled_tick: The tick before which nothing can be rolled back any more.
docs.start: On a host, start with whoever is in rather than waiting for `players`; false when there is no lobby to start.
docs.stats: `{ rtt_ms, loss, bytes_in, bytes_out }` for the link a slot is reached over; nil for this machine's own. An observer: never simulate from it.
docs.tick: The match tick being simulated; what a match branches on instead of `engine.tick`.

modules.doc: What every node has: name, path, transform, children, components and script. Each function takes the node first; scripts call it as a method, `self.node.get_node("Arm")`.

docs.add_child: Create a named child node under this one and return it.
docs.add_tag: File the node under a name; `scene.tagged` finds it from then on.
docs.attach_script: Attach the script at a path, with an optional table overriding what the script exports.
docs.authored: The component as a save writes it: every property it holds, an inline asset as its definition, a colour as `#rrggbb` where it is one, and no read-only property. Nil when the node does not carry it.
docs.call: Call a method on the node's script and return what it gives back; nil when there is no such script or method.
docs.call_async: Call a method that may suspend, and get a token `task.wait` resumes with its result once it returns: `task::wait(door.call_async("open")).await`, a GDScript `await door.open()`.
docs.children: The node's direct children, an empty list when it has none.
docs.component_names: The names of every component on the node.
docs.component_property: One property of the named component, nil when the node does not carry it: what a caller reading a single value should ask for.
docs.descendants: Every node under this one, in tree order, the node itself excluded.
docs.detach_script: Drop the script instance on this node, so no further lifecycle call reaches it; the node and its components stay.
docs.effective_tint: What the renderer multiplies by: this node's tint with every ancestor's folded in.
docs.emit: Emit an event from this node, delivered at the top of the next frame to whoever subscribed to `name` on this node, and to whoever subscribed to `name` from anyone. `call` is the twin that reaches one known script, now.
docs.free: Destroy the node and its subtree now, scripts detached first: what a tool editing a scene does, where no script of the subtree is running. A game frees with `queue_free`.
docs.get_component: The named component's properties as a table, nil when the node does not carry it.
docs.get_node: The node at an `A/B/C` path relative to this one, `..` climbing to the parent and a leading `/` starting from the root; nil when nothing matches.
docs.global_position: The node's position in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_rotation_euler: The node's world rotation as euler angles in radians, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_scale: The node's scale in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.has_component: Whether the node carries the named component.
docs.has_method: Whether the node's script declares this method, so a caller can tell "no handler" from "a handler that answered nothing".
docs.has_tag: Whether the node is filed under a name.
docs.instance: The prefab file the node instances, nil when it instances none.
docs.is_valid: Whether the node is still in the world; false rather than an error when the value is not a node.
docs.look_at: Turn the node so its -z, the way a camera and a light face, points at a world point, with +y up. It faces from where its `position` puts it now, under its parent's pose as of the last transform sync.
docs.material: The `material` asset the node names itself, empty when it takes its parent's.
docs.name: The node's own name, empty when it carries none.
docs.overrides: What the node changes of what the prefab that built it asks: a table by component of the properties it sets differently, and its script's under `script`. Empty for a node no prefab built.
docs.parent: The node's parent, nil at the root.
docs.patch_component: Change the properties the table names and leave the rest of the component where they were. On a node without the component this adds it, the schema defaults being what it currently holds. Answers whether the component took the values: one it refuses goes to the log with its reason, and the script goes on. A component or property nothing has, or a node that is gone, is an error.
docs.path: The node's slash-separated path, built by climbing parents from the node up to the root.
docs.process: When this node ticks: "inherit", "pausable", "always" or "disabled". "inherit" is the default and takes the nearest ancestor's answer.
docs.queue_free: Destroy the node and its subtree at the end of the frame.
docs.remove_component: Take the named component off the node.
docs.remove_tag: Take a name off the node; a name it never had is left alone.
docs.reset_interpolation: Throw away the poses the node was blending and start again from where it is, so a teleport does not streak across the level. `physics3d.teleport` and `physics2d.teleport` call it for you.
docs.script_field: A member the node's script instance holds, read by another script: GDScript's `node.speed`. Nil for no script or no such member.
docs.script_path: The path of the script the node names, nil when it names none; named whether or not it runs.
docs.script_props: What the node sets over its script's exported defaults, as a table; empty when it sets nothing.
docs.set_component: Give the node the named component, built from the given table over the component's schema defaults. Every property the table leaves out goes back to its default; `patch_component` is the one that changes a property and leaves the rest. A script hears every write to the scene, this one and a node added, freed, renamed or moved, with `events::listen(this.node, "changed")`, as `on_changed(entries)` at the top of the next frame.
docs.set_global_position: Put the node at a world point, Godot's `global_position = point`: it writes the `position` that lands there under its parent's pose as of the last transform sync, so `global_position` reads the point once the next sync has run. An axis a zero scale above flattens, or a point that is not finite, keeps the node's own coordinate.
docs.set_name: Rename the node, doing nothing when it carries no name.
docs.set_parent: Move the node under another, keeping where it is in the world; an error for a cycle or a dead parent.
docs.set_process: Set when the node and its subtree tick. "always" runs through a pause, which is what a pause menu is; "disabled" never runs; "inherit" goes back to the parent's. Physics is one world and is held whole by a pause whatever this says.
docs.set_script: Name the node's script and what it sets, without running it: what a scene's `script` key says and `attach_script` also starts. Nil takes the script off.
docs.set_sibling_index: Move the node to that place among its siblings, clamped to the end. Order is draw order in a `row` or a `column`, and tree order in the digest.
docs.set_state: Put the node in one of its `states`: the state's table is patched over the components it names, and `on_state_changed(from, to)` follows. A node already in that state is left alone.
docs.set_tint: Multiply a colour into everything the node and its subtree draw, alpha included, one meaning untinted. A renderable's own `color` is the node's alone; this is the one that inherits.
docs.set_visible: Show or hide the node and everything under it, emitting `visibility_changed` with the new value when the flag moves. Physics is untouched: a hidden collider still collides.
docs.set_z_index: Put the node and its subtree on a draw layer: higher draws later. It adds to the parent's layer unless `relative` is false, which makes it absolute.
docs.sibling_index: Where the node sits among its parent's children, counting from zero; 0 at the root.
docs.stable_id: The node's stable id: what a scene file declared, or what it was given when it was spawned. Survives rename and reparent, which a path does not.
docs.tags: The names the node is filed under, sorted.
docs.tint: The node's own tint as r, g, b, a channel floats; an ancestor's multiplies into it on the way to the screen.
docs.visible: Whether the node itself is set to draw; an ancestor may still hide it.
docs.visible_in_tree: What the renderer sees: false when the node or any ancestor is hidden.
docs.z_index: The node's own draw layer, added to its parent's unless set absolute.

modules.doc: What spans both physics worlds: pausing, sleeping, tuning and clearing. Bodies and colliders live in `physics2d` and `physics3d`.

docs.clear: Remove every body and collider from both worlds, as a play-in-editor session does on stop.
docs.counters: What each world's last step spent its time on. The first call turns rapier's profilers on, so the numbers arrive from the step after it.
docs.debug_draw: What the debug renderer is drawing now, every flag and `nodes` given.
docs.quarantined: What rapier disabled in each world's last step because a position, velocity or shape stopped being a number. Empty lists are the normal answer.
docs.set_debug_draw: Draw the physics world over the scene, as `modes` names it: `DebugDraw { colliders: true }` is the shapes, and `enabled: false` nothing. `[physics.debug]` holds the colours and lengths.
docs.set_paused: Stop or resume stepping both worlds; nodes keep their poses.
docs.set_sleeping_allowed: Allow or forbid resting bodies falling asleep, in both worlds and for bodies added later.
docs.set_tuning: Change how the solver behaves: `solver_iterations`, `length_unit`, `ccd_substeps`, contact softness, the `soft_*` rows and a `soft_recovery` record, the keys `[physics]` takes. A key at the top reaches both worlds; a `physics3d` or `physics2d` record holds keys for that world alone, which win over the top. Every value here changes results, so a recording only replays against the same numbers: prefer `[physics]`, `[physics.3d]` and `[physics.2d]` in project.toml.
docs.sleeping_allowed: Whether resting bodies are allowed to fall asleep.
docs.threads: How many threads the solver is using. One in a browser, unless the page is the threaded template and called `initThreadPool`.
docs.tuning: The solver settings each world is running with, every key `set_tuning` takes, `soft_recovery` included.
