modules.doc: The 2D rigid-body world: bodies and colliders on nodes, their velocities, raycasts and overlap queries. `physics` holds what spans both worlds.

docs.aabb: The world-space box the collider currently occupies, from its lowest corner to its highest.
docs.add_constant_force: Push the body every step until the constant force is set back to zero; unlike an impulse this is spread over time.
docs.add_constant_force_at_point: Push at a world point every step, which also turns the body.
docs.add_constant_torque: Turn the body every step until the constant torque is set back to zero.
docs.add_particle_force: Push one particle with `force` each step until `reset_forces`.
docs.add_softbody_force: Push every free particle with `force` each step until `reset_forces`.
docs.angular_velocity: How fast the body is spinning, in radians per second.
docs.apply_force: Push the body for the next step only; `add_constant_force` keeps pushing.
docs.apply_force_at_point: Push at a world point for the next step only, which also turns the body.
docs.apply_impulse: Add an instant change in momentum, as if the body were struck.
docs.apply_impulse_at_point: Strike the body at a world point, which spins it as well as moves it.
docs.apply_softbody_impulse: Change every free particle's velocity by `impulse` at once, as a kick to the whole body.
docs.apply_softbody_impulse_at_point: Strike the particles within `radius` of `point`, less the further they are; a radius of 0 strikes them all.
docs.apply_softbody_radial_impulse: Push the particles within `radius` away from `center`, as a blast does.
docs.apply_torque: Turn the body for the next step only; `add_constant_torque` keeps turning it.
docs.apply_torque_impulse: Add an instant change in angular momentum, as if the body were spun.
docs.attach_particle: Tie one particle to a node's rigid body where it is now: the body and the particle pull on each other.
docs.broad_phase_aabb: The box the broad phase files the collider under, which also reaches ahead by its body's speculative_distance.
docs.closest_point: The closest point on any collider to a world point.
docs.closest_points: The nearest point on each of two nodes' colliders; nothing when they overlap.
docs.collider_mass_properties: What this collider adds to its body, in its own space.
docs.collider_mesh: A voxel collider's outline as points and the segments between them, for drawing it or for spawning the pieces it broke into.
docs.collider_volume: How much area the shape encloses.
docs.collision_aabb: The box the narrow phase tests the collider in: its shape's box grown by its collision_margin and the world's prediction distance.
docs.combine_voxels: Tell two voxel colliders on one lattice about each other's cells, so a body sliding from one onto the other does not catch on the seam. Both must share a cell size and a rotation.
docs.constant_force: The force every step integrates until it is set back to zero.
docs.constant_torque: The torque every step integrates until it is set back to zero.
docs.contacts: Every contact point on this node's collider this step. Empty for a sensor, which has no contacts by definition.
docs.crop_voxels: Empty every cell outside the cells from `(min_x, min_y)` to `(max_x, max_y)`, both included. A range holding no filled cell leaves the grid as it was.
docs.cut_softbody: Cut the body along a blade at once, as `crossing` reads it; answers a record for each piece it changed, the one `on_torn` hears.
docs.detach_particle: Untie one particle from every body it was attached to; answers whether it was attached.
docs.effective_angular_inertia: The inertia the solver turns: zero with rotation locked, and on any body that is not dynamic.
docs.effective_dominance: The dominance rapier will use for this body: its own group, or the rank every non-dynamic body outranks with.
docs.effective_mass: The mass the solver pushes against along each world axis: zero along a locked axis, and on any body that is not dynamic.
docs.handles: The rapier handles behind this node, its body and its colliders. For matching a log line against rapier's own output.
docs.has_pending_tears: Whether some edge or cell is marked to tear at the end of the next step.
docs.heightfield_hole: Whether a heightfield segment has no ground.
docs.intersects: Whether two nodes' colliders overlap right now, sensor or not.
docs.is_ccd_active: Whether the body moved fast enough last step for rapier to sweep it, with or without continuous_collision.
docs.is_moving: Whether the body is awake and actually going somewhere.
docs.is_sleeping: Whether the body is asleep and being skipped.
docs.is_softbody_sleeping: Whether the body has come to rest and stopped being simulated.
docs.joint_force: The force and the torque the joint held through the last step. An articulation has none to read, and says so.
docs.kinetic_energy: The body's kinetic energy, for a rest test the solver agrees with.
docs.linear_velocity: How fast the body is travelling, in units per second.
docs.local_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in the body's own space.
docs.max_contact_impulse: The hardest contact this body took in the last step, every collider on it included; zero when nothing touched it.
docs.move_character_by: Move the character by an offset, sliding along walls, climbing steps and staying on the ground. Every solid collider of the character is swept. Call it from fixed_update.
docs.next_position: The pose a kinematic body has been told to move to.
docs.overlap_aabb: Every collider whose bounds meet an axis-aligned box.
docs.overlap_point: Every collider containing a world point: what a mouse click asks.
docs.overlap_shape: Every collider a shape overlaps where it stands.
docs.overlaps: The nodes this one currently intersects; rapier reports a pair only when one of the two colliders is a sensor.
docs.pin_particle: Hold one particle where it is, which is how a cloth hangs from a hook.
docs.pose_in_body: Where the collider sits in its body's frame; nothing for a collider with no body.
docs.potential_energy: The body's gravitational potential energy over one step.
docs.predict_position: Where the body will be after `dt` seconds at its current velocity.
docs.predict_position_with_forces: The same, with the forces already applied taken into account: where a thrust or a spring will have put it.
docs.raycast: The first collider a ray meets, or nothing.
docs.raycast_all: Every collider a ray meets, nearest first.
docs.reset_follow: Forget what a `pid` follow summed, so it pulls from now as if it had just started.
docs.reset_plasticity: Undo every permanent set the body took: rest lengths, rest angles and rest shapes go back to how it was built, and it springs back from where it is.
docs.reset_softbody_forces: Take back every force `add_force` and `add_particle_force` gave the body.
docs.set_angular_velocity: Set how fast the body spins, in radians per second.
docs.set_cell_tear_resistance: The same for one cell's tear strain.
docs.set_constant_force: Replace the constant force with this one; zero stops the push.
docs.set_constant_torque: Replace the constant torque with this one; zero stops the turn.
docs.set_edge_tear_resistance: How many times the material's threshold one edge takes to tear; 1 is the material's.
docs.set_gravity: Set the 2D world's gravity, in units per second squared.
docs.set_heightfield_hole: Remove or restore one segment of a heightfield's ground, numbered from the first height.
docs.set_linear_velocity: Set how fast the body travels, in units per second.
docs.set_particle_damaged: Mark one particle as damaged or mend it: a damaged particle tears as an outside one does, which seeds where a crack starts.
docs.set_particle_position: Put one particle at `at` with no change of velocity.
docs.set_particle_target: Move a held particle to `at` over the next step, with the velocity that takes, which is how a cloth is dragged.
docs.set_particle_velocity: Set one particle's velocity; a held one keeps moving at it.
docs.set_voxel: Fill or empty one cell of a voxel collider: digging a hole, or building a wall, while the game runs.
docs.set_voxel_size: Resize every cell of a voxel collider, keeping which cells are filled.
docs.shapecast: Sweep a shape along a direction until it hits something: a thick raycast.
docs.sleep: Put the body to sleep now.
docs.softbody_area: How much area the body and every piece torn off it enclose right now, against `rest_area` for how far it is squeezed.
docs.softbody_attachments: Every particle tied to a rigid body.
docs.softbody_boundary: The body's surface as particle indices: segments in 2D, triangles in 3D.
docs.softbody_cells: Every cell as its particle indices: triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D.
docs.softbody_contacts: What the body's surface touched in the last step.
docs.softbody_crossing: The edges and cells a blade meets, without cutting: the blade is a segment's two points in 2D, a triangle's three in 3D.
docs.softbody_edges: Every edge as the two particle indices it joins, in the order `stress` reports them.
docs.softbody_effective_particle_radius: How thick the particles are: what was asked for, or what the layout worked out.
docs.softbody_particle_count: How many particles the body has, every piece torn off it included: a generator decides, not the author.
docs.softbody_rest_area: How much they enclose at rest.
docs.softbody_stress: Each edge's load as a fraction of its tear threshold, smoothed over `tear_smoothing`: 0 slack, 1 tearing; the larger of its stretch over `tear_strain` and its force over `tear_force`, and 0 while neither is set.
docs.softbody_total_mass: What the whole body weighs, every piece included.
docs.softbody_volume_pieces: Each closed piece of the surface whose volume is held; an open sheet has none.
docs.softbody_world_center_of_mass: The centre of mass of the body and its pieces, which is where it is when a deformable body has no one position.
docs.solve_ik: Move a reduced-coordinates chain so its last link reaches a world position, leaving every joint inside its limits. Options: `rotation` (radians to turn the link to), `constrain` (the world axes to match: `x`, `y`, `rotation`; the translation by default, every axis when `rotation` is given), `damping` (1.0), `iterations` (10), `tolerance` (0.001).
docs.swept_aabb: The box the collider covers over the next fixed step, from where it is to where its body's velocity and forces carry it.
docs.tear_cell: Tear one cell at the end of the next step: a particle near its middle splits across its main stretch.
docs.tear_edge: Tear one edge at the end of the next step.
docs.tear_softbody: Tear the given edges and cells at once; answers a record for each piece it changed, the one `on_torn` hears.
docs.teleport: Move the body to a world position at once, clearing its velocity: what assigning the node's position cannot do, because the step writes that back every tick. A `rotation` turns it too, in radians.
docs.time_of_impact: When two moving colliders would meet, given each one's velocity. Nothing when they never do.
docs.time_since_can_sleep: Seconds the body has spent under its sleep thresholds; it sleeps once this reaches time_to_sleep.
docs.total_inertia: The body's resistance to spin, colliders included.
docs.total_mass: The body's total mass: its `mass` when it states one, or what its colliders weigh.
docs.unpin_particle: Let a held particle go; it keeps the velocity it had.
docs.velocity_at_point: How fast a world point on the body is moving, spin included.
docs.voxel: Whether one cell of a voxel collider is filled.
docs.voxel_at: The cell a world position falls in, as two whole numbers.
docs.voxel_size: How big one cell of a voxel collider is, along each axis.
docs.wake_all: Wake every sleeping body in the 2D world.
docs.wake_up: Wake the body, so the next step moves it.
docs.wake_up_softbody: Start simulating a resting body again.
docs.world_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in world space.

docs.crop_voxels: Empty every cell outside the cells from `(min_x, min_y, min_z)` to `(max_x, max_y, max_z)`, both included. A range holding no filled cell leaves the grid as it was.
docs.cut_softbody: Cut the body along a blade at once, as `crossing` reads it; answers a record for each piece it changed, the one `on_torn` hears.
docs.detach_particle: Untie one particle from every body it was attached to; answers whether it was attached.
docs.effective_angular_inertia: The world-space inertia the solver turns, rotation locks applied, as its three rows.
docs.effective_dominance: The dominance rapier will use for this body: its own group, or the rank every non-dynamic body outranks with.
docs.effective_mass: The mass the solver pushes against along each world axis: zero along a locked axis, and on any body that is not dynamic.
docs.handles: The rapier handles behind this node, its body and its colliders. For matching a log line against rapier's own output.
docs.has_pending_tears: Whether some edge or cell is marked to tear at the end of the next step.
docs.heightfield_hole: Whether a heightfield cell has no ground.
docs.intersects: Whether two nodes' colliders overlap right now, sensor or not.
docs.is_ccd_active: Whether the body moved fast enough last step for rapier to sweep it, with or without continuous_collision.
docs.is_moving: Whether the body is awake and actually going somewhere.
docs.is_sleeping: Whether the body is asleep and being skipped.
docs.is_softbody_sleeping: Whether the body has come to rest and stopped being simulated.
docs.joint_force: The force and the torque the joint held through the last step: what `break_force` and `break_torque` are measured against. An articulation has none to read, and says so.
docs.kinetic_energy: The body's kinetic energy, for a rest test the solver agrees with.
docs.linear_velocity: How fast the body is travelling, in units per second.
docs.local_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in the body's own space.
docs.max_contact_impulse: The hardest contact this body took in the last step, every collider on it included; zero when nothing touched it.
docs.move_character_by: Move the character by an offset, sliding along walls, climbing steps and staying on the ground. Every solid collider of the character is swept. Call it from fixed_update. It reads the world the step just wrote.
docs.next_position: The pose a kinematic body has been told to move to.
docs.overlap_aabb: Every collider whose bounds meet an axis-aligned box; cheaper and looser than shape_hits.
docs.overlap_point: Every collider containing a world point.
docs.overlap_shape: Every collider a shape overlaps where it stands: an explosion's reach, a melee arc.
docs.overlaps: The nodes this one currently intersects; rapier reports a pair only when one of the two colliders is a sensor.
docs.pin_particle: Hold one particle where it is, which is how a cloth hangs from a hook.
docs.pose_in_body: Where the collider sits in its body's frame; nothing for a collider with no body.
docs.potential_energy: The body's gravitational potential energy over one step.
docs.predict_position: Where the body will be after `dt` seconds at its current velocity.
docs.predict_position_with_forces: The same, with the forces already applied taken into account: where a thrust or a spring will have put it.
docs.raycast: The first collider a ray meets, or nothing.
docs.raycast_all: Every collider a ray meets, nearest first.
docs.reset_follow: Forget what a `pid` follow summed, so it pulls from now as if it had just started.
docs.reset_plasticity: Undo every permanent set the body took: rest lengths, rest angles and rest shapes go back to how it was built, and it springs back from where it is.
docs.reset_softbody_forces: Take back every force `add_force` and `add_particle_force` gave the body.
docs.set_angular_velocity: Set how fast the body spins, in radians per second about each axis.
docs.set_brake: How hard this wheel brakes, as an impulse; ignored while its engine force is not 0.
docs.set_cell_tear_resistance: The same for one cell's tear strain.
docs.set_constant_force: Replace the constant force with this one; zero stops the push.
docs.set_constant_torque: Replace the constant torque with this one; zero stops the turn.
docs.set_edge_tear_resistance: How many times the material's threshold one edge takes to tear; 1 is the material's.
docs.set_engine_force: How hard this wheel drives, in newtons; negative reverses.
docs.set_gravity: Set the 3D world's gravity, in units per second squared.
docs.set_heightfield_hole: Remove or restore the ground of one heightfield cell, named by the row and column of its first corner.
docs.set_linear_velocity: Set how fast the body travels, in units per second.
docs.set_particle_damaged: Mark one particle as damaged or mend it: a damaged particle tears as an outside one does, which seeds where a crack starts.
docs.set_particle_position: Put one particle at `at` with no change of velocity.
docs.set_particle_target: Move a held particle to `at` over the next step, with the velocity that takes, which is how a cloth is dragged.
docs.set_particle_velocity: Set one particle's velocity; a held one keeps moving at it.
docs.set_voxel: Fill or empty one cell of a voxel collider: digging a hole, or building a wall, while the game runs.
docs.set_voxel_size: Resize every cell of a voxel collider, keeping which cells are filled.
docs.set_wheel_rotation: Set how far the wheel has turned about its axle, in radians: the angle `state` reads as `rotation`.
docs.shapecast: Sweep a shape along a direction until it hits something: a thick raycast, and how a camera avoids walls.
docs.sleep: Put the body to sleep now.
docs.softbody_attachments: Every particle tied to a rigid body.
docs.softbody_boundary: The body's surface as particle indices: segments in 2D, triangles in 3D.
docs.softbody_cells: Every cell as its particle indices: triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D.
docs.softbody_contacts: What the body's surface touched in the last step.
docs.softbody_crossing: The edges and cells a blade meets, without cutting: the blade is a segment's two points in 2D, a triangle's three in 3D.
docs.softbody_dihedrals: Every bending hinge between two surface triangles, as four particle indices: the shared edge, then the two opposite particles.
docs.softbody_edges: Every edge as the two particle indices it joins, in the order `stress` reports them.
docs.softbody_effective_particle_radius: How thick the particles are: what was asked for, or what the layout worked out.
docs.softbody_particle_count: How many particles the body has, every piece torn off it included: a generator decides, not the author.
docs.softbody_rest_volume: How much they enclose at rest.
docs.softbody_stress: Each edge's load as a fraction of its tear threshold, smoothed over `tear_smoothing`: 0 slack, 1 tearing; the larger of its stretch over `tear_strain` and its force over `tear_force`, and 0 while neither is set.
docs.softbody_total_mass: What the whole body weighs, every piece included.
docs.softbody_volume: How much space the body and every piece torn off it enclose right now, against `rest_volume` for how far it is squeezed.
docs.softbody_volume_pieces: Each closed piece of the surface whose volume is held; an open sheet has none.
docs.softbody_world_center_of_mass: The centre of mass of the body and its pieces, which is where it is when a deformable body has no one position.
docs.solve_ik: Move a reduced-coordinates chain so its last link reaches a world position, leaving every joint inside its limits. Options: `rotation` (euler radians to turn the link to), `constrain` (the world axes to match: `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotation_x`, `rotation_y`, `rotation_z`; the translation by default, every axis when `rotation` is given), `damping` (1.0), `iterations` (10), `tolerance` (0.001).
docs.swept_aabb: The box the collider covers over the next fixed step, from where it is to where its body's velocity and forces carry it.
docs.tear_cell: Tear one cell at the end of the next step: a particle near its middle splits across its main stretch.
docs.tear_edge: Tear one edge at the end of the next step.
docs.tear_softbody: Tear the given edges and cells at once; answers a record for each piece it changed, the one `on_torn` hears.
docs.teleport: Move the body to a world position at once, clearing its velocity: what assigning the node's position cannot do, because the step writes that back every tick. A `rotation` turns it too, in Euler radians.
docs.time_of_impact: When two moving colliders would meet, given each one's velocity. Nothing when they never do.
docs.time_since_can_sleep: Seconds the body has spent under its sleep thresholds; it sleeps once this reaches time_to_sleep.
docs.total_inertia: The body's resistance to spin about each of its principal axes, colliders included.
docs.total_inertia_rotation: How those principal axes are turned in the body's own space, as Euler radians as `rotation_euler` reads them.
docs.total_mass: The body's total mass: its `mass` when it states one, or what its colliders weigh.
docs.unpin_particle: Let a held particle go; it keeps the velocity it had.
docs.vehicle_speed: How fast the chassis is going along its forward axis, in units per second.
docs.velocity_at_point: How fast a world point on the body is moving, spin included.
docs.voxel: Whether one cell of a voxel collider is filled.
docs.voxel_at: The cell a world position falls in, as three whole numbers.
docs.voxel_size: How big one cell of a voxel collider is, along each axis.
docs.wake_all: Wake every sleeping body in the 3D world.
docs.wake_up: Wake the body, so the next step moves it.
docs.wake_up_softbody: Start simulating a resting body again.
docs.wheel_state: What the last step did with this wheel.
docs.world_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in world space.

modules.name: physics3d

signatures.crop_voxels: (Node, int, int, int, int, int, int)

modules.doc: A picture of a project: its scene through its current camera, at its `[window]` size, written to a PNG by a second process running `balaur run --offscreen --shot`.

docs.write: Write a picture of the project at `project`, of `scene` (project-relative; its main scene when empty), as the files on disk say. Answers where the PNG will be: `[export] output`'s `picture` folder, or beside the project's manifest. The `picture_event` event reports it, `{ kind: "written", path }` or `{ kind: "failed", path, message }`. Nil where no second process can run, as in a browser tab.

modules.name: picture

modules.doc: Store services every platform shares: sign-in, achievements, leaderboards, cloud saves, purchases, a sign-in page in the OS's own sheet, local notifications and push. A call answers `task::wait` later with a map whose `kind` is `signed_in`, `signed_out`, `done`, `scores`, `read`, `identity`, `web_sign_in`, `notifications`, `scheduled`, `push_registered`, `push_failed`, `products`, `purchased`, `pending`, `entitlements`, `restored`, `finished`, `cancelled`, `error` or `unsupported`, each an `EVENT_*` constant. What arrives unasked is the `platform_event` event, `events::listen(node, "platform_event")`: a sign-in or sign-out, a notification or a push tapped (`notification_opened`), one shown in front (`notification_received`) or a push that reached the game in front (`push_received`), a push token the OS replaced (`push_token_changed`), and a purchase that landed with nobody asking (`transaction`). `is_available` says whether a service works here. A test answers calls from the file `BALAUR_STAND_INS` names.

docs.backend: The name of the loaded store, or "none".
docs.cancel_notification: Drop a scheduled notification, and take a delivered one out of the shade.
docs.close_web_sign_in: Shut the sign-in page `web_sign_in` opened, once the game has what it opened it for: its call answers `cancelled`, and on Android the game comes back to the front over the tab.
docs.cloud_read: Read a value the store syncs between the player's devices, and return the id whose `read` answer holds it as `value`: a string, or nil when the key holds nothing. On Play Games it is a saved game named `key`, and a conflict between two devices' saves resolves to the one modified last.
docs.cloud_write: Write a value for the store to sync between the player's devices, and return the id its answer carries. On Play Games it is a saved game named `key` (letters, digits and `-._~`, up to 100), and a save another device made that Play has not reconciled with this one's is refused with `error`, never overwritten: read it, then write again.
docs.entitlements: What this player owns now: return the id whose `entitlements` answer holds them as `items`, each a `Transaction`.
docs.finish_purchase: Tell the store a purchase is dealt with, once a server has checked its `token`, and return the id its `finished` answer carries. One never finished comes back on every launch, and Play refunds one unacknowledged after three days.
docs.identity: Ask the store for a proof of who is playing that a server checks with it, and return the id whose `identity` answer carries it: Steam's Web API ticket as `ticket`, hex, for `ISteamUserAuth/AuthenticateUserTicket`; Play Games' one-time server code as `code`, for `[google] server_client_id`, which the server exchanges with Google.
docs.is_available: Whether a service works on this device in this run, named by a `SERVICE_*` constant: the store or OS answers, a recording's answer in a replay, false where nothing reaches it.
docs.notify: Schedule a local notification, and return the id its `scheduled` answer carries. A tap brings the game forward and is the `platform_event` event, `notification_opened` with the `id` and `data`; one shown while the game is in front is `notification_received`.
docs.player: Who the store says is playing, or nil before a sign-in has landed.
docs.products: Ask the store about a list of product ids, and return the id whose `products` answer holds what it knows, each a `Product`. An id the store does not know is left out.
docs.progress: Report an achievement's completion, 0 to 100, and return the id its answer carries.
docs.purchase: Buy a product in the store's own sheet, and return the id its answer carries: `purchased` with the `Transaction`'s fields, `cancelled` or `pending` with `product`, or `error`. A pending one lands later as `transaction` on `platform_event`.
docs.register_for_push: Ask the OS for this device's push token, and return the id whose `push_registered` answer carries it as `token`, with `provider` (`PUSH_PROVIDER_APNS` or `PUSH_PROVIDER_FCM`) and `platform` (`PUSH_PLATFORM_IOS`, a Mac's too, or `PUSH_PLATFORM_ANDROID`): the three fields Gamend's `push_tokens::register_push_token` takes, so the answer is handed to it as it is. `push_failed` says why with `error`, naming the capability to add when the export left it out (`[apple] capabilities = ["push-notifications"]`, `[android] capabilities = ["firebase-messaging"]`); `unsupported` elsewhere. A token the OS replaces later is `push_token_changed` on `platform_event`, with the same fields. Showing a push needs `request_notifications` first, as a local notification does.
docs.request_notifications: Ask the player to allow notifications, and return the id whose `notifications` answer says what they said as `allowed`. On Android 13 and later this is the system's permission prompt.
docs.restore_purchases: Ask the store to hand this player's purchases back, the button a review expects a game to have, and return the id its `restored` answer carries; read them with `entitlements` after.
docs.scores: Read a leaderboard's entries, and return the id whose `scores` answer holds them as `entries`, each a `Score`.
docs.set_presence: Say what the player is doing, where the store shows it, and return the id its answer carries.
docs.sign_in: Ask the store who is playing, and return the id its answer carries. A later sign-out is the `platform_event` event.
docs.submit_score: Post a score to a leaderboard, and return the id its answer carries.
docs.unlock: Award an achievement whole, and return the id its answer carries.
docs.web_sign_in: Open a sign-in page in the OS's own sheet over the game (a Custom Tab on Android), and return the id its answer carries: `web_sign_in` with the `url` it ended on when it reached `opts.scheme`, `cancelled` when shut, `unsupported` where the platform has no such sheet (open the page with `engine::open_url` there).
docs.web_sign_in_state: How the page `web_sign_in` opened last stands, without waiting: `PAGE_NONE` before any, `PAGE_OPEN` while it has not answered, else the `kind` it answered. A game polling a server meanwhile reads it to hear the player shut the page.

modules.name: platform

modules.doc: The projects this machine has opened, the templates a new one starts from, and the folder picker the OS provides. What the editor's start screen is made of.

docs.copy: Copy the project folder at `from`, one `fs.*` may read, to `into`, which must not exist yet, and remember the copy. Answers `{ path, name }`, or `{ error }`.
docs.copy_system_font: Copy an installed face, one `system_fonts` lists, to `to` inside the project. Answers whether it was copied; a path the list does not name is refused.
docs.create: Write a new project at `path` from a template id, or from nothing when the id is empty. Answers `{ path, name }`, or `{ error }`.
docs.examples_directory: The folder of example projects shipped beside the editor, which `fs.*` may read and not write from then on. Nil where none ship.
docs.exists: Whether anything is at `path`, wherever it is: how a new project's folder is picked clear of one already there.
docs.forget: Drop one project from the list. The folder is not touched.
docs.home: Where a new project goes unless the reader says otherwise: the home directory on a desktop, and the app's own writable directory where there is no such thing.
docs.in_tab: Whether this editor runs in a browser tab, where the page holds the projects and opening one is its call rather than this screen's.
docs.open: Remember `path` and start the editor on it, then ask this one to quit. Answers `{ error }` when there is no project there.
docs.open_beside: Start a second editor on `path` and keep this one: Edit dependency on a `path` dependency, whose project is another folder. Answers `{ error }` when there is no project there or no second editor can start.
docs.pick_directory: Open the OS folder picker and answer what was chosen, or `()` when it was dismissed. Blocks while the dialog is up, and answers `()` on a platform with no picker.
docs.recent: The projects opened on this machine, newest first: `{ path, name, opened, exists }` each, where `opened` is a Unix time in seconds and `exists` says whether the folder is still there.
docs.system_fonts: The faces this machine has installed, by family and style: what the font picker offers to copy into a project, since an exported game cannot count on a face being installed. Empty in a browser tab.
docs.use_data: Answer `engine::user_data_directory()` with the user data directory of the game named `name`, keep the device id there, and let `fs` reach it, so a game played here and run alone share saves and a device login. The editor names its own folder with `engine::user_data_directory_of`. Nil goes back to the editor's own. Answers the directory, or nil.
docs.version: The version of the binary the editor is running in.

modules.name: project

modules.doc: Rotations as quaternions `{ x, y, z, w }`: from an axis and an angle, from one direction to another or from a `rotation_euler`, composed, inverted and applied to a vector. Balaur Script over glam's formulas, so every platform turns alike.

docs.from_arc: The shortest turn that takes the direction `from` onto `to`.
docs.from_axis_angle: A turn of `angle` radians about `axis`, which need not be unit length.
docs.from_euler: A transform's `rotation_euler`, in radians, as a quaternion.
docs.mul: `b`, then `a`: the composed rotation, as a child's turn under its parent's is `mul(parent, child)`.
docs.to_euler: A quaternion as the `rotation_euler` a transform takes, in radians.

modules.name: quat

modules.doc: The engine's one deterministic PCG32 stream: the same seed draws the same numbers on every platform, and a replay reproduces every draw.

docs.at: The `index`th number of the stream `seed` names, uniform in `[0, 1)`: the same for the same two on every platform, and apart from the engine stream, so a tool's layout draws nothing a game would.
docs.float: A float from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[0, 1)`.
docs.int: A whole number from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[low, high]`, both ends included.
docs.range: A float from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[low, high)`: the two arguments.
docs.seed: Restart the deterministic engine stream at the given seed, so every draw after it repeats.
docs.uuid: A version-4 UUID drawn from the deterministic engine stream, so a replay makes the same ids; not for anything that must be unique across machines.

modules.name: random

modules.doc: Regular expressions, the `regex-lite` dialect: no look-around or back-references. A pattern is compiled on every call; a match is a `Match`, with byte offsets and one string per capture group, nil for a group that took no part.

docs.escape: `text` with every metacharacter escaped, so it matches itself.
docs.matches: Whether the pattern matches anywhere in `text`.
docs.replace: `text` with the first match replaced, or every match when `all` is true; `$1` and `${name}` in `with` stand for groups.

modules.name: regex

modules.doc: Which build of the engine this is, what the channels are publishing, and replacing this install with another. The editor's Engine tab and About sheet; `balaur update` is the same code.

docs.channels: Every release line a build may follow, in the order a version moves through them.
docs.check: Read the release feed on a thread. `release_event` hears `{ kind: "listed", rows }`, newest first, each `{ tag, id, channel, when, current, order, download }`: `order` is `newer`, `older` or `same` than this build, empty where they do not order, and `download` is the zipped app a macOS bundle fetches instead. `{ kind: "failed", job: "check", message }` when the feed could not be read. False while a recording plays.
docs.install: Replace this install with what that channel or tag holds, on a thread; `allow_downgrade = true` lets an older build replace a newer one. `release_event` hears `downloading` with `done` and `total` bytes, `unpacking`, then `installed` with a `note`, or `failed` with `job: "install"`. Refuses where `installed().held` says why. False while a recording plays.
docs.installed: This build: `{ version, id, channel, tag, source, held }`, where `id` is the build id a release was tagged with, `tag` is the release its assets live under, `source` is true for a build from a checkout, and `held` says why this install cannot replace itself, empty when it can.

modules.name: release

modules.doc: What a frame is made of: the shape, sprite, mesh or emitter a node draws, the 2D and 3D cameras, the backdrop, debug lines and screenshots. `window` holds the window itself.

docs.begin_retained: Keep what is drawn from here to `end_retained` under `key`, drawn every frame until the key is drawn again or cleared: an overlay redrawn when what it shows moves, not each frame.
docs.bounds: The box the node's geometry covers in its own space, as a centre xyz and half-extents xyz, with a z of zero for a 2D node; nil for a node that draws nothing. A solver's body reports where it is now, not where it was built; a text, the lines it was last laid out in.
docs.built_mesh: The triangles the node's boolean settled on, ready to be written out as a `mesh` asset; nil when the node draws no built geometry.
docs.camera_2d: The 2D camera this frame: its `center` and its `zoom` in logical pixels per world unit; all zeros with no window.
docs.camera_matrix: The camera's projection*view matrix this frame, 16 numbers column-major; all zeros with no window.
docs.camera_pose: The camera the renderer actually used, which is where a backend put it and not what a `camera3d` asked: its `eye` and `target`, the vertical `fov` in radians and the HiDPI `scale_factor`. Zeros and a scale of one with no window.
docs.cell: The tile at a column and row, or -1 for an empty cell or one past the edge.
docs.cell_terrain: The terrain value painted at a column and row, or -1 where nothing was painted.
docs.check_material: Every diagnostic about the material at that path, as `[{ file, line, column, severity, message }]`; empty when it links.
docs.clear_retained: Stop drawing what `key` kept. A script hears the camera a frame was drawn with move, to draw a group sized in pixels again, with `events::listen(this.node, "camera_moved")`.
docs.debug_view: Which channel the viewport is drawing instead of the scene's colour, or empty for the scene as it is.
docs.debug_views: Every channel name `set_debug_view` accepts, as a list.
docs.draw_arc_2d: Stroke an arc between two angles in radians, counter-clockwise from the x axis, for this frame; width is in pixels, and `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_box_3d: Draw a wireframe box centred at a point, `size` across along each axis in world units, for this frame.
docs.draw_capsule_3d: Draw a wireframe capsule centred at a point, `height` being the straight part along y, for this frame.
docs.draw_circle_2d: Fill a circle in world units for this frame, over everything the scene drew; `opts.z_index` places it among the nodes of that index instead.
docs.draw_lines_3d: Draw 3D world-space lines for this frame, each with its own ends, colour, width, `perspective` and `on_top`: a frame's worth crosses to the engine once.
docs.draw_polygon_2d: Fill a convex outline of world-space points for this frame; `geometry2d` cuts a concave one into triangles first. `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_polyline_2d: Stroke a chain of world-space points for this frame; width is in pixels, and `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_rect_2d: Fill a rectangle of `size` centred at `position`, in world units, for this frame; `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_sphere_3d: Draw a wireframe sphere centred at a point, as three rings in world units, for this frame.
docs.draw_text_2d: Draw a line of text in 2D world space for this frame, shaped by the engine's fonts. `opts` takes the `text2d` keys (`font_size`, `font_weight`, `font_style`, `color`, `text_align`, `markup`, `max_width`, `font`, `text_style`, …), `pixels_per_unit` and `z_index`; `font` and `text_style` name an asset.
docs.draw_text_3d: The same in 3D world space, on a quad that faces the camera. `pixels_per_unit` sizes it, so text a metre away reads the same whatever the font size.
docs.draw_texture_2d: Draw a project image over a rectangle of `size` centred at `position`, in world units, for this frame; the colour tints it. `opts` takes `z_index`, and `region_origin` and `region_size` in the image's pixels for part of it.
docs.end_retained: Keep what was drawn since `begin_retained` under its key, in place of what the key held.
docs.hold_cameras: Let no camera under a node drive the view, whatever its `current` says, until it is called with nil: an editor looking at a game through its own camera. The cameras keep what the scene asked of them.
docs.is_on_screen: Whether any of the notifier's box was on screen at the end of the last frame.
docs.material_params: The material's editable rows, one `{ name, type, value }` per field its linked shader declares; empty when it will not link.
docs.mouse_ray: The picking ray through the mouse position, in world units: where it starts and which way it goes.
docs.mouse_world_2d: The mouse position in 2D world coordinates, for picking.
docs.outline: The outline this node blocks 2D light with, as its points in world space, with the first repeated at the end when the outline is closed. Empty on a node with no `occluder2d`.
docs.pick_ray_at: The nearest node with a 3D shape that a world-space ray meets, from its origin along its direction, as `node` and `at`, how far along the ray it was met; nil when the ray meets nothing.
docs.screenshot: Save the next rendered frame as a PNG at a project-relative path. `screenshot_saved` goes to every listener with the path once it is on disk, and `screenshot_failed` with `{ path, error }` when it cannot be, a run with no renderer included.
docs.set_background: Set the colour the viewport is cleared to behind everything drawn: the colour a `#rrggbb` writes, each channel from 0 to 1. Its alpha is not read.
docs.set_cell: Put one tile at a column and row; a tile below zero clears the cell, and a cell outside the map grows it in that direction. The mesh rebuilds on the next frame.
docs.set_cell_terrain: Paint a terrain value at a column and row and let the tileset's rules pick the tiles, for that cell and the ring around it; below zero clears it.
docs.set_debug_view: Draw one channel of the scene (normals, uv, depth or albedo) instead of its colour; an empty name puts the picture back.
docs.set_shader_preview: Draw the value a shader's line computes for every pixel that reaches it; line 0 puts the picture back.
docs.snap_aov: Render the 3D scene once more as `render.AOV_DEPTH` (nearest brightest), `AOV_NORMALS` (world space), `AOV_CAMERA_NORMALS` or `AOV_SEGMENTATION` (a colour per object) and save it as a PNG, announcing it as `screenshot` does. A read-back of the GPU, as `screenshot` is.
docs.stats: What this frame draws: `{ draws, triangles, texture_bytes, textures, nodes }`, where `nodes` is a row per node that drew, each `{ node, draws, triangles, texture_bytes, copies }`. Presentation, never simulation: nothing in the digest reads it.
docs.text_size: The width and height `text` shapes to, in font pixels, with the project's own fonts and never a system face, so a run with no window open answers as a windowed one does. A width is presentation: writing one into state puts presentation in the digest.
docs.texture_pixels_per_unit: How many of an image's pixels make a world unit when a sprite says 0: its own `pixels_per_unit` import setting, else 100.
docs.texture_size: An image's width and height in pixels, read from the file's own header.
docs.trace_texture: The outline of an image's opaque pixels, as `[x, y]` points in a node's own space, ready to be a polygon's `positions`. `opts` takes `threshold` (alpha counted as opaque, 0 to 1, default 0.5), `tolerance` (how many pixels of detail to drop, default 2), `pixels_per_unit` (default 100) and `holes` (every loop, largest first: each other island counter-clockwise and each hole clockwise; default false keeps the largest alone). Counter-clockwise with y up, centred on the origin, the way a sprite at the same `pixels_per_unit` is drawn.
docs.triangles_of: The triangles `node` draws, from its mesh, its shape or its 2D polygon, as three corners each in the space of `space`, or of the world where it is left out.
docs.view_point: The point of the world a `camera2d` drawing into a `view` shows at `at`, in the window's design pixels as `ui::widget_rect` and `view_clicked` give it; nil while its view is not drawn, or in a run with no window.

modules.doc: Records what a running game is fed and plays it back. A recording holds each tick's input, network arrivals and events; `balaur run --record` writes one.

docs.divergence_tick: The first tick whose replay did not reproduce the recorded digest, or nil.
docs.events: The events recorded between two ticks, each with its tick, kind, label and data.
docs.header: The loaded recording's project, start time, script fingerprint, its frame count and the ticks they span, and how it ended; nil with none loaded.
docs.info: The same summary for a recording on disk, without loading it. Nil when it cannot be read.
docs.load: Read a recording and put it in front of the engine, paused before its first tick. Nil when it cannot be read, which is logged.
docs.marks: The ticks at which one replay source held a non-empty list under a key, and what it held.
docs.pause: Stop between ticks, holding the simulation still while the frame loop keeps drawing.
docs.play: Run the loaded recording, one recorded tick per frame.
docs.record: Start recording into a file; call it before the code it records runs. Answers the path, or nil when the file cannot be written, which is logged.
docs.recording: The file being recorded into, or nil.
docs.recording_name: A file-safe name for a recording starting now, so a list of them sorts by when they ran.
docs.seek: Run recorded ticks until playback reaches the given tick; forward only.
docs.stop: Close the recording, naming why it ended, and return the file it wrote.
docs.unload: Drop the loaded recording and let the game run live again.

modules.doc: Rollback netcode from a script's side. `input` reads this tick's input, real or predicted; `is_resimulating` is true when a tick runs again after a late input.

docs.input: What that player is doing on the tick being simulated, real or predicted; nil outside a session or for a player it does not know.
docs.is_resimulating: Whether this tick is a re-run of one already simulated, so a script can skip anything it must not do twice.

modules.doc: The node tree: its root, lookup by path and instancing, plus the component vocabulary an editor's palette lists.

docs.attach_scripts: Run every script the nodes under a node name, children first: what starts a scene built with `scripts: false`.
docs.bindable_events: Every event a `[[nodes.bindings.rows]]` row may answer, in the order an editor offers them: the core hooks, and on a node the `emitted:` events it, its components and its script announce.
docs.binding_actions: Every action a binding row may do, in the order an editor offers them.
docs.component_expects: The components a component type needs something from, for ordering or grouping its sections; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_properties: What a component's `apply` would receive for `params`: the schema's defaults with a partial table merged over them. This is how a tool compares two spellings of the same component.
docs.component_schema: A component type's property schema as a table, its properties in the order it writes them; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_tags: The facets a component type is filed under, for filtering a palette; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_types: The names of every registered component type, not the components on any node.
docs.current: The root of the scene the last `switch`, or the run's start, built under a node, the tree's root when nil; no node while none stands there.
docs.instantiate: Build a scene document (TOML text, not a path) under a parent. `scripts: false` names each node's script without running it; `root` is the project the text names its files from, when it is not this one, and every path is made absolute against it; under a node of the content the engine plays, that project is the default.
docs.keep_changes: Keep every change under a node as it happens, each with what it replaced, until `take_changes` hands them over; nil stops, and what was kept goes. An editor's undo, which the `changed` event serves a frame late and merged.
docs.node_by_id: The node carrying a stable id, which survives the rename and the reparent a path does not; nil when nothing carries it. `under` bounds the search to one subtree, for a tool holding more than one tree.
docs.preload: Ready a scene before a switch to it: its file and every prefab under it read and parsed now, and the pictures they name decoding on a worker thread. No node is built and nothing in the world changes, so a replay that never preloaded builds the same world. An error when a file does not read or parse, said now rather than at the switch.
docs.preloaded: Whether a scene `preload` readied is ready to show: its file and every prefab under it read, and every picture they name decoded and on the GPU, so its first frame draws it whole with nothing decoded on that frame. Ask it after `preload` until it answers true, a frame or a `task::frames` apart. An error when a file does not read or parse.
docs.repeat: One instance of each item's scene file under `host`, in the items' order after the host's other children, and the instance's root for each. An instance is kept from call to call: the same key keeps its node, a new key takes a spare of the same scene, and an instance no item asks for is hidden, not freed, so a list asked for every pass builds only when it grows. Each root is named for its item's `key`, so a binding row handing over the node says which item it is; a spare is named `spare0`, `spare1` and on. An instance's stable ids are the file's under `<host id>/<n>/`, as a prefab instance's are. A scene file with more than one root is an error, as are two items sharing a key and a key that is empty or holds a `/`.
docs.set_variable: Write a scene variable, coerced to the type it was declared with. Every node declaring `on_variable_changed` hears about it at the end of the tick; writing the value it already holds says nothing.
docs.switch: Go to another scene at the end of this tick, so a script asking inside `update` is not moving the tree it runs in. The scene the last switch built under `under` is freed, each of its scripts' `on_free` running, and `path` is built there new, every `init` running: a visit always starts fresh, and a switch to the file already there is a reset. `under` is the tree's root when nil, where the main scene stands; only that scene's own root goes, so a node a script made beside it under the same parent stays and keeps running. `fade` is seconds of crossover: the old scene's root fades out to the clear colour over the first half, the switch happens, and the new one fades in over the second. A scene `preload` warmed builds from its caches; one it did not is read on the frame.
docs.tagged: Every node filed under a tag, in tree order; what a scene's `tags` key and `node.add_tag` feed.
docs.take_changes: The changes kept since the last take, oldest first, emptying the list: `{ node, kind, id }` with `kind` one of `component` (`component`, `properties`, `was`: the table asked before), `attached`, `removed` (`was`), `added` (`parent`), `freed` (`parent`, `place`, `was`: the subtree as scene text), `renamed` (`was`), `moved` (`parent`, `was`: `{ parent, place }`), `script` (`was`: `{ source, props }`, nil for none) and `keys` (`was`: every one of the node's own keys, `visible` to `tags`). Parents are stable ids, so a change outlives the nodes it names.
docs.to_toml: The scene under a node, that node its root, as a scene file's text: what `instantiate` builds again. Each component is what was asked of it, a prefab's nodes are their instance's `overrides`, and `root` writes every path under that project's root as it spells it.
docs.unload: Let go of what `preload`, or a pack warming its scenes, readied: the parsed text of the file and its prefabs, and the pictures they name. A scene standing stays where it is, and a picture something still draws is read again when it next asks.
docs.variable: A scene variable's value, or nil for a name nothing declared. A scene declares them under `[variables]`.
docs.variables: Every declared variable as `{ name, type, value }`, in name order.
docs.warnings: What is off about the node, as `{ component, property, message }`: a component missing one it expects, a write its component refused, and what a component says of itself. `property` is nil for the whole component; advisory only.
docs.with_component: Every node carrying the named component, in tree order. What a script asks instead of walking the tree itself.

modules.doc: What a tool asks about a script file. The editor and `balaur check` have it; a game's runtime does not.

docs.api: Every module a script can reach: its functions, their signatures and what each does, and its constants.
docs.check: Every compiler error in the source, read as the file at the path: one for each function that does not compile.
docs.complete: Every completion valid at that caret; an editor passes the buffer it is showing.
docs.definition: Where the name at that caret is declared in the file; nil when it is not.
docs.exports: Every `pub` field of the script's class, which a scene tunes, in the order the file declares them: its `name` and its spec, `type` and `default`, with `of`, `fields`, `options`, `variants` or `description` where they apply.
docs.find: Every place that text appears in the file, matched as text rather than as a name.
docs.format: The source laid out as `balaur fmt` lays it out; unchanged when it will not parse.
docs.hover: What the name at that caret is: its type, or its signature; nil when it is nothing.
docs.references: Every use of that name in the file.
docs.rename: The file with a name renamed; nothing is written, so a caller can show it first.
docs.replace: The file with that text replaced; nothing is written, so a caller can show it first.
docs.signature: The call the caret is inside, and which argument it is on.
docs.symbols: What the file declares: its structs, their fields and methods, its functions, and each `event` with its description for a detail.

modules.doc: A small secret kept by the OS, by key: a session's refresh token. Apple's Keychain, an Android Keystore key sealing each value, the Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service on Linux (`secret-tool`), else a file under the user directory only this user may read. A page keeps it in `localStorage`, which any script on the page can read: not secure. Read and written in the call, and never recorded. A test keeps them in that file with `"secrets.backend": "file"` in the file `BALAUR_STAND_INS` names.

docs.backend: Where this run keeps its secrets, a `BACKEND_*` constant.
docs.get: What `key` holds, or nil where it holds nothing or the store cannot be read.
docs.remove: Forget what `key` holds. False where it held nothing.
docs.set: Keep `value` under `key`, over what it held. False where the store refused, with the reason logged.

modules.doc: Every setting the engine, its plugins and the game declare, by path: `physics/solver_iterations` is `[physics] solver_iterations` in `project.toml`. `define` adds your own; `[override.<platform>]` tables answer per platform.

docs.all: Every defined setting as `{ path, scope, spec }`, in definition order.
docs.base: What the file says, ignoring every override: what a settings screen edits.
docs.clear: Forget one value, so the next write drops the key: how an override is removed.
docs.define: Declare a setting of your own: `type`, `default`, and optionally `min`, `max`, `options`, `help`, `order` and `applies`. A path starting `editor/` is kept on this machine; anything else ships with the game.
docs.get: One setting's value here: the narrowest `[override.<tag>]` this platform answers to, else what was set, else what its definition defaults to, else nil.
docs.known_tags: Every tag a project may write an override for: the engine's, then the project's own from `[export] tags`.
docs.merge_toml: Read values out of a TOML text, folding them onto what is already loaded.
docs.overrides: The tags this project holds an override for at `path`, in tag order.
docs.set: Change one setting, in memory. Whether it takes effect now or on the next run is the setting's own business; `all` reports it as `applies`.
docs.to_toml: The text one scope would write, starting from `existing` so anything no setting describes survives. Scope is "project" or "editor".

docs.bones: The bones under the node in tree order, the order a skin numbers them in, the node itself first when it is one.
